INSTITUTIONS: Institution(s): The European Securities and Markets Authority (ESMA)
DESCRIPTION: ESMA, in its advice, has assessed the level of consideration of Environmental, Social and Governance (ESG) factors in both specific credit rating actions, and the credit rating market in general.

TITLE: The United Kingdom's Green Finance Strategy
INSTITUTIONS: Institution(s): Government of the United Kingdom
COUNTRY: Country: United Kingdom of Great Britain and Northern Ireland
DESCRIPTION: The United Kingdom's Green Finance Strategy, which is published under the Green Finance Initiative, recognises the role of the financial sector in delivering global and national climate and environmental objectives. It aims to ensure that climate and environmental factors are fully integrated into mainstream financial decision-making across all sectors and asset classes. It also introduces new initiatives such as the development of a new global biodiversity framework and a commitment to work with international partners to improve nature-related financial disclosures.

TITLE: Proposed Amendment to Regulation No. 1092/2010 Would Direct the European Systemic Risk Board to Monitor and Assess Environmental and Social Risks
DESCRIPTION: On 16 April 2019, the European Parliament proposed an amendment to Regulation No. 1092/2010 that would direct the European Systemic Risk Board (ESRB) to monitor and assess environmental and social risks.

TITLE: TCFD Consortium of Japan
INSTITUTIONS: Institution(s): Japanese Financial Services Agency (JFSA), the Japanese Ministry of Economy, Trade and Industry (METI) and the Ministry of the Environment (MOE)
DESCRIPTION: The consortium is designed to facilitate corporate information disclosures on climate change and aimed at encouraging financial institutions to make investments based on climate risks.

TITLE: Hong Kong Green Bond
INSTITUTIONS: Institution(s): The Hong Kong Monetary Authority
DESCRIPTION: Hong Kong sold a five-year U.S. dollar-denominated green bond with a coupon of 2.5%, attracting over $4 billion in orders from investors globally.

TITLE: European Union Guidelines on Reporting Climate-Related Information
DESCRIPTION: In June 2019, the European Union (EU) published a supplement to the 2017 guidelines on non-financial reporting in order to provide companies with guidance on reporting climate-related information.

TITLE: French Banking Groups Facing Climate Change-Related Risks
INSTITUTIONS: Institution(s): Autorité de contrôle prudentiel et de résolution (ACPR)
DESCRIPTION: Today there is a growing recognition of climate change-related risks by risk management functions, underlining the fact that these issues are now considered beyond the CSR function. This evolution is reflected in some institutions by an increasing quantification of risks and exposures and early sensitivity analyses of portfolios.

TITLE: Moscow Exchange to establish Sustainability Sector
DESCRIPTION: The Moscow Exchange Listing Rules created a Sustainability Sector for financing projects in the fields of environmental and social sustainability. The sector consists of three independent segments: green bonds, social bonds and national projects.

TITLE: Guidelines on Disclosure Requirements Applicable to Credit Ratings Include Environmental, Social, and Governance (ESG) Considerations
INSTITUTIONS: Institution(s): The European Securities and Markets Authority (ESMA)
DESCRIPTION: The European Securities and Markets Authority (ESMA) has developed guidelines on disclosure requirements for credit ratings in order to improve the overall quality and consistency of credit rating agencies’ (CRAs’) consideration of environmental, social and governance (ESG) factors in their ratings.

TITLE: Roadmap for Aligning the Moroccan Financial Sector with Sustainable Development
DESCRIPTION: The Roadmap for Aligning the Moroccan Financial Sector with Sustainable Development outlines proposed measures for the banking sector, insurance sector, and capital markets to promote sustainable finance and take into account concerns related to environmental, social, and governance (ESG) issues, including climate change.

TITLE: Morocco's Sustainable Insurance Strategy
INSTITUTIONS: Institution(s): Autorite de Controle des Assurances et de la Prevoyance (ACAPS)
DESCRIPTION: Morocco's Supervisory Authority of Insurance and Social Welfare (Autorité de Contrôle des Assurances et de la Prévoyance Sociale, or ACAPS) is now developing a strategy for the implementation of the National Roadmap into the insurance sector, including promoting sustainable insurance (i.e. membership of UN PSI), development of incentive schemes, and other activities.

TITLE: Hong Kong Announced Responsible Investment measures as part of Three Sets of Measures on Green Finance Development
INSTITUTIONS: Institution(s): The Hong Kong Monetary Authority (HKMA)
DESCRIPTION: The Hong Kong Monetary Authority (HKMA) unveiled three sets of measures to support and promote Hong Kong's green finance development during the HKMA Green Finance Forum on 7 May 2019, including a principle that priority will be given to Green and ESG investments if the long term return is comparable to other investments on a risk-adjusted basis.

TITLE: European Commission Draft Rules Aim to Ensure That Investment Firms and Insurance Distributors Consider Sustainability When Advising Clients
DESCRIPTION: On 4 January 2019, the European Commission published draft rules on how investment firms and insurance distributors should take sustainability issues into account when providing advice to their clients.

TITLE: Regulation (EU) 2019/2088 of the European Parliament and of the Council of 27 November 2019 on sustainability‐related disclosures in the financial services sector (the Disclosure Regulation - SFDR)
DESCRIPTION: As part of the European’s Commission’s Action Plan ‘Financing Sustainable Growth’, the Regulation (EU) 2019/2088 of the European Parliament and of the Council of on sustainability-related disclosures in the financial services sector was published on 9 December 2019 in the Official Journal of the European Union (the Disclosure Regulation). The main aim of the Disclosure Regulation is to provide more transparency to end-investors on whether and how the buyside and financial advisers take into account ESG aspects.

TITLE: Regulation (EU) 2019/1238 on a Pan-European Personal Pension Product (PEPP)
DESCRIPTION: Regulation (EU) 2019/1238 on a Pan-European Personal Pension Product (PEPP) enables the creation of a personal pension product that will take into account environmental, social, and governance (ESG) factors.

TITLE: Regulation (EU) 2019/2089 of the European Parliament and of the Council of 27 November 2019 amending Regulation (EU) 2016/1011 as regards EU Climate Transition Benchmarks, EU Paris-aligned Benchmarks and sustainability-related disclosures for benchmarks
DESCRIPTION: As part of the European’s Commission’s Action Plan ‘Financing Sustainable Growth’, the Regulation (EU) 2019/2089 (the Low Carbon Benchmark Regulation) requires all benchmark providers administrating benchmarks to disclose whether and how they take ESG factors into account.

TITLE: Hong Kong established the Centre for Green Finance (GCF) under the HKMA Infrastructure Financing Facilitation Office (IFFO)
INSTITUTIONS: Institution(s): The Hong Kong Monetary Authority (HKMA)
DESCRIPTION: The Hong Kong Monetary Authority (HKMA) unveiled three sets of measures to support and promote Hong Kong's green finance development during the HKMA Green Finance Forum on 7 May 2019, including the Centre for Green Finance (CGF), established under the HKMA Infrastructure Financing Facilitation Office (IFFO)

TITLE: The Dutch Authority for the Financial Markets' 2019 Agenda - Supervision in Transition
INSTITUTIONS: Institution(s): The Netherlands Authority for the Financial Markets (Autoriteit Financiële Markten), AFM)
DESCRIPTION: The Dutch Authority for the Financial Markets (AFM) has published its 2019 Agenda, which takes into account the transition to a sustainable society and economy as well as AFM's monitoring of compliance with information disclosure obligations, including non-financial information, by companies.

TITLE: Technical Advice to the European Commission on Integrating Sustainability Risks and Factors into the Markets in Financial Instruments Directive II (MiFID II)
INSTITUTIONS: Institution(s): The European Securities and Markets Authority (ESMA)
DESCRIPTION: The European Securities and Markets Authority (ESMA) has prepared technical advice for the European Commission (EC) on integrating sustainability risks and factors into the Markets in Financial Instruments Directive II (MiFID II).

TITLE: European Parliament legislative resolution of 18 April 2019 on the proposal for a regulation of the European Parliament and of the Council on disclosures relating to sustainable investments and sustainability risks and amending Directive (EU) 2016/2341
DESCRIPTION: The European Union (EU) Regulation on Sustainability-Related Disclosures in the Financial Services Sector provides harmonised rules on transparency and disclosure in relation to financial market participants' integration of sustainability risks and the consideration of adverse sustainability impacts in their processes, as well as the provision of sustainability-related information on financial products.

TITLE: EBA 2020 mandates to consider ESG factors
DESCRIPTION: On October 2019, the European Banking Authority published its detailed annual work programme for 2020 which states its contribution to the sound development of financial innovation and sustainability.

TITLE: Abu Dhabi Securities Exchange creates ESG disclosure guidance for listed company
DESCRIPTION: Abu Dhabi Securities Exchange (ADX) issued an Environmental, Social and Governance (ESG) disclosure guidelines for listed companies.

TITLE: Russia’s Environmental Permitting Regime is Revised in Government Decree No. 143
INSTITUTIONS: Institution(s): The Ministry of Natural Resources and the Environment of the Russian Federation
DESCRIPTION: Russia's environmental permitting regime was revised in January 2019 with the adoption of Decree No. 143.

TITLE: Technical Advice on the Integration of Sustainability Risks in Insurance Undertakings and Products in the European Union
INSTITUTIONS: Institution(s): The European Insurance and Occupational Pensions Authority (EIOPA)
DESCRIPTION: The European Insurance and Occupational Pensions Authority (EIOPA) has provided technical advice on the integration of sustainability risks in European Union (EU) insurance undertakings and products, including underwriting practices and investment decisions.

TITLE: The Netherlands Responded to a Global Survey on Implementation of the Recommendations of the Task Force on Climate-Related Financial Disclosures (TCFD)
DESCRIPTION: The Netherlands has responded to a global survey by the Sustainable Insurance Forum (SIF), which has uncovered significant differences among many insurers’ and reinsurers’ levels of awareness, uptake, and implementation of the Recommendations of the Task Force on Climate-Related Financial Disclosures (TCFD).

TITLE: BaFin Perspectives Special Study on Sustainability Issues
DESCRIPTION: BaFinPerspectives examines strategic supervisory and regulatory issues from different angles.

TITLE: The Central Bank of Hungary’s Green Program
DESCRIPTION: The Central Bank of Hungary ("MNB") launched its Green Program 2019 to mitigate the risks associated with climate change and other environmental problems, to expand green financial services in Hungary, to widen the related knowledge base in Hungary and abroad, and to reduce financial market participants’ and its own ecological footprint.

TITLE: New Investment Guidelines for Sweden’s Pension Fund Include Higher Ambition Level on Sustainability
INSTITUTIONS: Institution(s): Third Swedish National Pension Fund (AP3)
DESCRIPTION: In January 2019, Sweden’s Pension Fund adopted new Investment Guidelines that imply a higher ambition level regarding sustainability.

TITLE: Opinion on Sustainability within Solvency II – Integrating Climate Risks in Investment and Underwriting Practices of (Re)insurers
INSTITUTIONS: Institution(s): The European Insurance and Occupational Pensions Authority (EIOPA)
DESCRIPTION: The European Insurance and Occupational Pensions Authority (EIOPA) prepared an opinion on sustainability within Solvency II, which aims to integrate sustainability and climate risks in the investment and underwriting practices of (re)insurers.

TITLE: The Netherland Issued a Sovereign Green Bond
INSTITUTIONS: Institution(s): The Dutch State Treasury Agency (DSTA)
DESCRIPTION: In May 2019, the Dutch State Treasury Agency (DSTA) issued a 20-year green bond. The Netherlands was the first country with a triple-A rating to issue a green bond.

TITLE: BaFin Guidance Notice on Dealing with Sustainability Risks
DESCRIPTION: The objective of this Guidance Notice is to provide entities supervised by BaFin with guidance on dealing with the increasingly important issue of sustainability risks.

TITLE: Athens Stock Exchange publishes ESG Reporting Guide
DESCRIPTION: ATHEX ESG Reporting Guide is a voluntary reporting guide is intended to function as a tool with which companies can identify the ESG issues they should consider disclosing and managing, on the basis of their impact on long-term performance. It also offers practical guidelines on the metrics companies should use to disclose this information and communicate it to relevant stakeholders.

TITLE: Singapore Responded to a Global Survey on Implementation of the Recommendations of the Task Force on Climate-Related Financial Disclosures (TCFD)
DESCRIPTION: Singapore has responded to a global survey by the Sustainable Insurance Forum (SIF), which has uncovered significant differences among many insurers’ and reinsurers’ levels of awareness, uptake, and implementation of the Recommendations of the Task Force on Climate-Related Financial Disclosures (TCFD).

TITLE: Widening of the Protection Gap for Natural Catastrophe Risks in the European Union Discussed at Workshop on Sustainable Finance
INSTITUTIONS: Institution(s): The European Insurance and Occupational Pensions Authority (EIOPA)
DESCRIPTION: On 11 June 2019, the European Insurance and Occupational Pensions Authority (EIOPA) organized a discussion with stakeholders on sustainable finance. Among the key areas of discussion was on the widening of the (insurance) protection gap for natural catastrophe risks.

TITLE: Phase 2 of the Reserve Bank Act Review Considers How Climate Risks Could Affect Financial Stability
INSTITUTIONS: Institution(s): Reserve Bank of New Zealand
DESCRIPTION: In June 2019, New Zealand published Phase 2 of a review of the Reserve Bank of New Zealand Act of 1989. The goal of the review is to modernise New Zealand’s monetary and financial stability policy frameworks and the Reserve Bank’s governance and accountability settings, including the role of the Reserve Bank in assessing and responding to climate risks.

TITLE: Regulatory Framework to Grow Green Finance
INSTITUTIONS: Institution(s): The Astana International Finance Centre (AIFC)
DESCRIPTION: The Astana International Finance Centre (AIFC) is developing a framework to facilitate the growing green finance sector in Kazakhstan.

TITLE: Ghana Sustainable Banking Principles
DESCRIPTION: The Bank of Ghana, in partnership with the International Finance Corporation (IFC), initiated the creation of a national platform in April 2015 and inaugurated a sustainable Banking Committee on 20th of November 2015 to start the development of sustainable banking principles.

TITLE: Kingdom of Thailand’s Guidelines for Responsible Lending
DESCRIPTION: In collaboration with 15 commercial banks, the Bank of Thailand will establish guidelines for responsible lending as part of its sustainable business operation.

TITLE: Specifications for 2019 Stress Test of Institutions for Occupational Retirement Provision (IORPs) Include Environmental, Social, and Governance Risks
INSTITUTIONS: Institution(s): The European Insurance and Occupational Pensions Authority (EIOPA)
DESCRIPTION: The European Insurance and Occupational Pensions Authority (EIOPA) published a document that describes the specifications for the 2019 stress test for institutions for occupational retirement provision (IORPs) that includes, for the first time, an assessment of IORPs' exposure to environmental, social, and governance (ESG) risks, including climate change.

TITLE: New Zealand Responded to a Global Survey on Implementation of the Recommendations of the Task Force on Climate-Related Financial Disclosures (TCFD)
INSTITUTIONS: Institution(s): Reserve Bank of New Zealand (RBNZ)
DESCRIPTION: New Zealand has responded to a global survey by the Sustainable Insurance Forum (SIF), which has uncovered significant differences among many insurers’ and reinsurers’ levels of awareness, uptake, and implementation of the Recommendations of the Task Force on Climate-Related Financial Disclosures (TCFD).

TITLE: Singapore's Green Investments Programme
DESCRIPTION: The Monetary Authority of Singapore (MAS) announced that it has set up a US$2 billion green investments programme (GIP) to invest in public market investment strategies that have a strong green focus.

TITLE: The UAE Responded to a Global Survey on Implementation of the Recommendations of the Task Force on Climate-Related Financial Disclosures (TCFD)
DESCRIPTION: The UAE has responded to a global survey by the Sustainable Insurance Forum (SIF), which has uncovered significant differences among many insurers’ and reinsurers’ levels of awareness, uptake, and implementation of the Recommendations of the Task Force on Climate-Related Financial Disclosures (TCFD).

TITLE: Guidelines for the issuance of Social, Green and Sustainable Securities
INSTITUTIONS: Institution(s): Panama Stock Exchange (Bolsa de Valores de Panama)
DESCRIPTION: The purpose of the Guidelines is to provide the market with best practices and parameters for the issuance of SGS securities aimed to spread international standards and guidelines to assess eligible assets.

TITLE: Japan Responded to a Global Survey on Implementation of the Recommendations of the Task Force on Climate-Related Financial Disclosures (TCFD)
DESCRIPTION: Japan has responded to a global survey by the Sustainable Insurance Forum (SIF), which has uncovered significant differences among many insurers’ and reinsurers’ levels of awareness, uptake, and implementation of the Recommendations of the Task Force on Climate-Related Financial Disclosures (TCFD).

TITLE: EU Sub-group on ESG Disclosures for Insurance-Based Investment Products
INSTITUTIONS: Institution(s): The European Insurance and Occupational Pensions Authority (EIOPA)
DESCRIPTION: The Joint Committee of European Supervisory Authorities has established a sub-group on ESG disclosures, which aims to develop technical standards on the disclosure of sustainability risks and investments in insurance-based investment products (IBIPs).

TITLE: Singapore's Green Finance Action Plan
DESCRIPTION: In 2019, the Monetary Authority of Singapore (MAS) announced the development of a new and comprehensive long-term strategy to make sustainable finance a defining feature of Singapore's role as an international financial centre. Built on three core pillars—building resilience, developing markets, and leveraging technology—the Green Finance Action Plan will be articulated through actions in six areas.

TITLE: South Africa Responded to a Global Survey on Implementation of the Recommendations of the Task Force on Climate-Related Financial Disclosures (TCFD)
DESCRIPTION: South Africa has responded to a global survey by the Sustainable Insurance Forum (SIF), which has uncovered significant differences among many insurers’ and reinsurers’ levels of awareness, uptake, and implementation of the Recommendations of the Task Force on Climate-Related Financial Disclosures (TCFD).

TITLE: Sustainability Reporting Guidelines for Publicly-Listed Companies
INSTITUTIONS: Institution(s): Philippines Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC)
DESCRIPTION: The Guidelines is intended to help PLCs assess and manage non-financial performance across Economic, Environmental and Social aspects of their organization

TITLE: The European Investment Bank's Draft Energy Lending Policy
DESCRIPTION: The European Investment Bank’s (EIB's) Draft Energy Lending Policy (ELP) focuses on activities in areas that it can provide a high degree of additional value: (i) filling investment gaps, (ii) focusing on long-term infrastructure needs, including innovation and scaling up low-carbon technologies, and (iii) supporting new market-based investments.

TITLE: Roadmap for Sustainable Finance In Georgia
DESCRIPTION: In April 2019, the National Bank of Georgia (NBG) launched the Roadmap for Sustainable Finance. The Roadmap summarizes all possible changes that the NBG intends to implement regarding the sustainable finance development in the near future with the corresponding timeframe.

TITLE: Indonesia's Green Bond and Green Sukuk Framework Helped Catalyse USD 2 Billion in Green Projects
DESCRIPTION: In 2018, Indonesia developed a Green Bond and Green Sukuk Framework under which it will finance or refinance Eligible Green Projects that contribute to the country's objectives of reducing greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions, adapting to climate change, and preserving biodiversity.

TITLE: Review of Issuers' Disclosure of Climate-Related Risks and Financial Impacts (CSA Staff Notice 51-354)
DESCRIPTION: The Canadian Securities Administrators (CSA) published CSA Staff Notice 51-354 in 2018 to report on the findings of a project to review the disclosure of risks and financial impacts to issuers associated with climate change, and the governance processes related to them.

TITLE: Eswatini's National Development Plan 2019/20 - 2021/22
INSTITUTIONS: Institution(s): Ministry of Economic Planning and Development of Eswatini
DESCRIPTION: In 2019, the Ministry of Economic Planning & Development of the Kingdom of Eswatini published the National Development Plan (NDP) 2019/20 - 2021/22.

TITLE: Australia Updates Guidance on Climate-Related Disclosure
DESCRIPTION: In 2019, the Australian Securities and Investments Commission (ASIC) published updates to clarify the application of its existing regulatory guidance on the disclosure of climate change related risks and opportunities.

TITLE: Sustainable Finance Principles
INSTITUTIONS: Institution(s): The Association of Banks in Cambodia (ABC)
DESCRIPTION: In February 2019, ABC issued the Cambodia Sustainable Finance Principles and its Implementation Guidelines, a voluntary framework to help banks integrate sustainability considerations into lending operations.

TITLE: Indonesia Issued US$1.25 Billion Green Sukuk
DESCRIPTION: In March 2018, the Government of Indonesia issued its first sovereign Green Sukuk in US dollars. The five-year issuance raised US$1.25 billion and reached a broad range of investors, including conventional, Islamic, and green investors.

TITLE: Environmental, Social, and Governance (ESG) Disclosure Requirements Included in Amendment to the United Kingdom's Occupational Pension Schemes Regulation
COUNTRY: Country: United Kingdom of Great Britain and Northern Ireland
DESCRIPTION: In 2018 and 2019, the United Kingdom introduced regulations with a suite of disclosure requirements to defined benefit and defined contribution pension schemes, aiming to further integrate Environmental, Social, and Governance (ESG) factors and disclosure into standard pension reporting requirements.

TITLE: National Bank of Rwanda's Regulation on Publication of Financial Statements and Other Disclosures
DESCRIPTION: The National Bank of Rwanda (NBR) requires banks to prepare integrated report integrating social, environmental and economic aspects.

TITLE: Korea is Developing Green Bond Guidelines
INSTITUTIONS: Institution(s): Ministry of Finance and Strategy
DESCRIPTION: Korea's Ministry of Finance and Strategy is developing Green Bond Guidelines.

TITLE: The Reserve Bank of Australia's Deputy Governor Calls for Incorporating Climate Models in Economic Modelling
DESCRIPTION: In 2019, the Reserve Bank of Australia's Deputy Governor delivered a speech about how climate change affects the objectives of monetary policy and financial stability.

TITLE: Green Bond Grant Scheme
DESCRIPTION: Hong Kong's Green Bond Grant Scheme (GBGS), announced on 15 June 2018, will subsidise eligible green bond issuers in obtaining certification under the Green Finance Certification Scheme (GFCS).

TITLE: Review of the Impact of Climate Change on the UK Banking Sector
COUNTRY: Country: United Kingdom of Great Britain and Northern Ireland
DESCRIPTION: A survey of 90 percent of the UK banking sector, representing more than £11 trillion in assets, found that the majority of banks are beginning to treat the risks from climate change like other financial risks, rather than viewing them simply as a corporate social responsibility issue.

TITLE: Nasdaq Copenhagen's Environmental, Social, and Governance (ESG) Data Portal
DESCRIPTION: Nasdaq Copenhagen's Environmental, Social, and Governance (ESG) Data Portal was created in 2018 to provide a central database, compilation, and repository for listing companies and investors alike to access ESG and performance metrics.

TITLE: Sustainable Finance Protocol
INSTITUTIONS: Institution(s): Banco de la Nación Argentina, Banco Galicia, Banco Ciudad, Banco BICE, Banco Supervielle, Banco CMF, Santander, Banco Provincia de Buenos Aires, BBVA, Banco Macro, HSBC Bank, Banco Patagonia, Banco Itau, Banco Comafi, Banco Industrial, Banco Mariva, Banco de Tierra del Fuego and Banco BST.
DESCRIPTION: A group of 18 banks have signed a Sustainable Finance Protocol in Argentina, with the aim of facilitating and encouraging financial institutions in the country to implement best practices and international policies that promote the integration of economic, social, and environmental factors.

TITLE: Financial Stability Report - Article on Climate-Related Risks and Sustainable Finance
DESCRIPTION: This article on Climate-Related Risks and Sustainable Finance details the findings of a survey conducted by the National Bank of Belgium (NBB), which shows that the awareness of financial institutions regarding climate-related risks is still at the early stages and that there is a lack of available data within institutions to adequately assess the exposure of Belgian institutions to climate-related risks.

TITLE: Changes to Iceland's Act on Natural Catastrophe Insurance (Act 55/1992) in 2018 Include Increased Minimum Deductibles and Requirement to Repair
INSTITUTIONS: Institution(s): Natural Catastrophe Insurance of Iceland (NTI)
DESCRIPTION: The purpose of Iceland's Natural Catastrophe Insurance (Act 55/1992) is to insure against direct losses incurred on account of volcanic eruptions, earthquakes, rock slides, avalanches, and floods. Changes to the Act in 2018 include, among other things, an increase in minimum deductibles and a requirement that the policy-holder use the compensation to repair/reconstruct the damaged item.

TITLE: The United Kingdom's Green Finance Task Force Issued Recommendations on Accelerating Green Finance
COUNTRY: Country: United Kingdom of Great Britain and Northern Ireland
DESCRIPTION: The United Kingdom's Green Finance Task Force published a report in 2018 that provides a series of recommendations on how the government and the private sector can work together to make green finance an integral part of the country's financial services.

TITLE: Rio Declaration on Climate Risk Transparency by the Brazilian Insurance Industry
INSTITUTIONS: Institution(s): Brazilian Insurance Confederation and Brazilian Superintendence of Private Insurance
DESCRIPTION: Brazilian Insurance Confederation and Brazilian Superintendence of Private Insurance signed in May 2018 a declaration stating that: "We believe that climate risk transparency is essential to better managing the impact of climate related risks on the insurance industry, and to promoting sustainable insurance markets."

TITLE: Focus Group Established to Discuss and Support the Implementation of Austria’s Green Finance Agenda
INSTITUTIONS: Institution(s): Austrian Federal Ministry of Finance and the Austrian Federal Ministry for Sustainability and Tourism
DESCRIPTION: Austria’s Green Finance Agenda was launched in February 2019, with a kick-off event and the establishment of a green finance focus group made of up the country’s key financial sector players.

TITLE: Belgium Responded to a Global Survey on Implementation of the Recommendations of the Task Force on Climate-Related Financial Disclosures (TCFD)
DESCRIPTION: Belgium has responded to a global survey by the Sustainable Insurance Forum (SIF), which has uncovered significant differences among many insurers’ and reinsurers’ levels of awareness, uptake, and implementation of the Recommendations of the Task Force on Climate-Related Financial Disclosures (TCFD).

TITLE: Luxembourg Establishes the World's First Legal Framework for Green Covered Bonds
DESCRIPTION: On 22 June 2018, Luxembourg established the world's first legal framework for green covered bonds (Law of 22 June 2018, amending the Law of 5 April 1993) to finance the generation of renewable energies.

TITLE: Danish Guidelines on Responsible Investment
DESCRIPTION: The Danish Guidelines on Responsible Investment aim to help clarify the expectations as to how Danish institutional investors should act in the context of responsible investment.

TITLE: Brazil's Investment Rules of Occupational Pension Funds Requires Asset Managers to Consider Environmental, Social, and Governance (ESG) Risks
DESCRIPTION: Brazil's Investment Rules of Occupational Pension Funds (Resolution CMN 4.661/2018) requires pension funds’ asset managers to consider environmental, social, and governance (ESG) risks as part of their investment decision making process.

TITLE: Australian Government Regulatory Bodies Say Climate Change Must Be Considered a Major Financial Risk and Call for More Disclosure
INSTITUTIONS: Institution(s): Australian Securities and Investments Commission (ASIC) and the Australian Prudential Regulatory Authority (APRA)
DESCRIPTION: In 2019, senior officials from the Australian Securities and Investments Commission (ASIC) and the Australian Prudential Regulatory Authority (APRA) said that the effects of climate change no longer presented merely ethical issues for Australian businesses but must be considered a major financial risk.

TITLE: Chile has Issued the First Sovereign Green Bond in the Americas
DESCRIPTION: In June 2019, Chile issued a USD 1.42 billion sovereign green bond, the first ever issued in the Americas.

TITLE: Luxembourg's Climate Finance Accelerator
INSTITUTIONS: Institution(s): Ministries of Finance and Sustainable Development and Infrastructure
DESCRIPTION: Luxembourg's Climate Finance Accelerator is a joint initiative by the government and private actors that aims to enhance the climate finance ecosystem by creating an attractive and supporting environment for climate finance fund managers in Luxembourg.

TITLE: Finland's Responsible Investments Standards
DESCRIPTION: In 2018, the Bank of Finland introduced responsible investment standards to the management of its investment portfolio.

TITLE: Voluntary Disclosure of Environmental, Social, and Governance (ESG) Information in Brazil – Updates on "Report or Explain for Sustainability or Integrated Reports"
INSTITUTIONS: Institution(s): Brazilian Securities and Exchange Commission (CVM)
DESCRIPTION: The Brazilian Stock Exchange (B3) has announced two updates since its “report or explain” approach was launched in 2012 to encourage listed companies to voluntarily disclose whether or not

TITLE: Warsaw Stock Exchange ESG Index
DESCRIPTION: In August 2019, Warsaw Stock Exchange launched an equity index that includes 60 of the largest and most-liquid securities that are assigned ESG scores using insights from Sustainalytics.

TITLE: Australian Sustainable Finance Initiative
DESCRIPTION: The Australian Sustainable Finance Initiative (ASFI), which was launched in March 2019, brings together leaders spanning Australia’s major banks, superannuation funds, insurance companies, financial sector peak bodies, and academia to develop a Sustainable Finance Roadmap, in consultation with diverse sectors and stakeholders.

TITLE: Malaysia's Value-Based Intermediation (VBI) Financing and Investment Impact Assessment Framework
DESCRIPTION: Malaysia's Value-Based Intermediation (VBI) Financing and Investment Impact Assessment Framework provides guidance to facilitate the implementation of an impact-based risk management system for assessing the Islamic Banking Institutions' (IBIs) financing and investment activities in line with their respective VBI commitment.

TITLE: Green and Sustainable Finance Cluster Germany
INSTITUTIONS: Institution(s): Hessian Ministry of Economics and Deutsche Börse
DESCRIPTION: The goal of the Green and Sustainable Finance Cluster Germany is to establish forward thinking and efficient financial market structures based on the implementation of sustainable financing strategies.

TITLE: Guidelines for Corporate Governance of Listed Companies in China
DESCRIPTION: In 2018, the China Securities Regulatory Commission (CSRC) published a revision of its Guidelines for Corporate Governance of Listed Companies, which establishes the framework for environmental, social, and governance (ESG) information disclosure.

TITLE: Survey Finds Increasing Awareness of and Action on Climate-Related Financial Risks by Australian Regulated Entities
DESCRIPTION: A climate change survey conducted by the Australian Prudential Regulation Authority (APRA) finds increasing awareness of and action on climate-related financial risks by regulated entities.

TITLE: Sustainability Disclosure Guide for Boursa Kuwait Listed Issuers
DESCRIPTION: In December 2019, Boursa Kuwait developed a sustainability disclosure guidance with the aim to support Kuwait listed issuers to report on Environmental, Social, and Governance (ESG) issues.

TITLE: Responsible Investment Charter of the Banque de France
DESCRIPTION: The Banque de France’s Responsible Investment Charter reflects the Bank’s aim to be exemplary in the inclusion of CSR in all its forms—economic, social, and environmental—across the management of assets for which it has the full and sole responsibility.

TITLE: Morocco's Sustainable Finance Module
INSTITUTIONS: Institution(s): The Moroccan Capital Market Authority
DESCRIPTION: A new sustainable finance module was launched in 2018 as part of the Moroccan Capital Market Authority's (L’Autorité Marocaine Du Marché Des Capitaux, or AMMC) professional licensing framework.

TITLE: China's Compulsory Environmental Pollution Liability Insurance
DESCRIPTION: In 2018, the China Insurance Regulatory Commission (CIRC), together with the Chinese Ministry of Environmental Protection (MEP), passed the Compulsory Environmental Pollution Liability Insurance (CEPLI) Regulation.

TITLE: Memorandums on Climate Change and the Duties of Company Directors in Australia
INSTITUTIONS: Institution(s): The Centre for Policy Development and Future Business Council
DESCRIPTION: Australia's Centre for Policy Development has issued two memorandums on climate change and the duties of company directors—one in 2016 and another in 2019.

TITLE: Illinois Sustainable Investing Act (2019), HB 2460
DESCRIPTION: The Illinois Sustainable Investing Act (2019), HB 2460, requires “all state and local government entities that hold and manage public funds to integrate material, relevant, and useful sustainability factors into their policies, processes, and decision-making”.

TITLE: Japan Corporate Governance Code
DESCRIPTION: Japan's Corporate Governance Code establishes fundamental principles for corporate governance at listed companies in Japan with a view to attaining sustainable corporate growth and increased corporate value over the mid- to long-term.

TITLE: China's Green Investment Guidelines
INSTITUTIONS: Institution(s): The Asset Management Association of China and the China Securities Regulatory Commission
DESCRIPTION: In 2018, the Asset Management Association of China issued Green Investment Guidelines to establish basic principles and standards for green investment methodologies, strategies, regulations, benchmarks, and evaluations.

TITLE: Banque de France's 2018 Responsible Investment Report Shows Strong Non-Financial Performance
DESCRIPTION: In 2018, the Banque de France conducted the first analysis of the extra-financial performance of its portfolios.

TITLE: Bangladesh's Green Transformation Fund (GTF)
DESCRIPTION: Bangladesh Bank’s Green Transformation Fund (GTF)—a USD 200 million refinancing scheme for environmentally-friendly initiatives launched in 2016—expanded its scope in June 2019 from just three sectors (textiles, leather, jute) to include all manufacturing and export-oriented entities, irrespective of sector.

TITLE: Myanmar Climate Change Strategy
INSTITUTIONS: Institution(s): Ministry of Natural Resources and Environmental Conservation (MONREC)
DESCRIPTION: Myanmar’s Climate Change Strategy (2018-2030) was published by the Government of the Republic of the Union of Myanmar in 2019. This strategy was formulated to provide long-term direction and guidance for government, civil society, and the private sector to undertake and promote climate change actions in adaptation and mitigation in Myanmar and to create opportunities for sustainable and low-carbon development..

TITLE: Japan's Environmental Reporting Guidelines
INSTITUTIONS: Institution(s): Government of Japan, Ministry of the Environment, Japan (MOEJ)
DESCRIPTION: Japan's 2018 Environmental Reporting Guidelines constitute a framework for international regulations, practical trends, and integrated environmental reporting. It requires reporting of both conventional environmental management information and forward-looking, non-financial data.

TITLE: China’s Green Bond Verification Guidelines
INSTITUTIONS: Institution(s): The People’s Bank of China (PBoC) and China Securities Regulatory Commission (CSRC)
DESCRIPTION: China's Green Bond Assessment and Verification Guidelines introduce regulatory requirements for verifiers, including the required qualifications and credentials, verification methods, and reporting requirements.

TITLE: Irish Sovereign Green Bond Framework
DESCRIPTION: The Irish Sovereign Green Bond Framework will enable Ireland to fund eligible Green Projects through the issuance of Irish Sovereign Green Bonds (ISGBs) in order to contribute to the country's commitment to transition to a low-carbon, climate resilient, and environmentally sustainable economy.

TITLE: Zimbabwe’s National Climate Change Response Strategy
INSTITUTIONS: Institution(s): Ministry of Environment, Ministry of Environment, Water and Climate of Zimbabwe
DESCRIPTION: In November 2019, the Government of Zimbabwe and Ministry of Environment, Water and Climate passed the National Climate Change Response Strategy.

TITLE: Green Finance Network Japan
DESCRIPTION: The Green Finance Network Japan (GFNJ) aims to facilitate multi-level stakeholder engagement and information sharing on green finance and to examine options for the reform of its financial system.

TITLE: Central Bank of Gambia’s objective of supporting sustainable economic growth
DESCRIPTION: The mandate of the Central Bank of Gambia includes an explicit objective for the promotion of sustainable economic development.

TITLE: Green Insurance to Support Afforestation
INSTITUTIONS: Institution(s): Superintendencia de Seguros de La Nación (SSN)
DESCRIPTION: Argentina's Superintendencia de Seguros de La Nación (SSN)—a decentralised body within the Ministry of Economy that advises the Executive on maters related to insurance market policy and oversees insurance and reinsurance entities—has implemented the Green Insurance Project, which allocates 1% of the premiums of automotive policies to support afforestation efforts.

TITLE: Egypt’s Financial Regulatory Authority Green Bond Guidelines
DESCRIPTION: Egypt’s Financial Regulatory Authority (FRA) approved the legal framework for issuing green bonds in July 2018, with the aim of providing financial tools to fund eco-friendly projects in the fields of new and renewable energy, construction, and transport.

TITLE: Italy Introduces Regulation that Highlights the Importance of Environmental and Social Factors in Insurance Undertakings (No. 38/2018)
INSTITUTIONS: Institution(s): Istituto per la Vigilanza Sulle Assicurazioni (IVASS)
DESCRIPTION: In 2018, Italy's Institute for the Supervision of Insurance (IVASS) introduced provisions in Regulation No. 38/2018 that underline the importance of social and environmental factors in the activities of insurance undertakings.

TITLE: Draft Amendment to Delegated Regulation 2017/2359 Aims to Integrate Environmental, Social, and Governance (ESG) Considerations into Advice on Insurance-Based Investment Products
DESCRIPTION: In 2018, the European Commission drafted an amendment to Delegated Regulation (EU) 2017/2359 to integrate Environmental, Social and Governance (ESG) considerations and preferences into the investment advice for insurance-based investment products.

TITLE: Indonesia Sustainable Finance Initiative
INSTITUTIONS: Institution(s): Bank Artha Graha Indonesia, BRI Syariah, Bank Central Asia, Bank Mandiri, Bank Muamalat, Bank Negara Indonesia, Bank Pembangunan Daerah Jawa Barat dan Banten, and Bank Rakyat Indonesia (supported by OJK)
DESCRIPTION: The Indonesia Sustainable Finance Initiative (ISFI) aims to promote and implement inclusive sustainable finance practices.

TITLE: Guiding Opinions of the China Securities Regulatory Commission on Supporting the Development of Green Bonds
DESCRIPTION: In 2017, China issued an Announcement (No. 6) to encourage relevant government departments and local governments to introduce preferential policy measures to support the development of green bonds.

TITLE: Technical Advice on Amendments to European Directives (2009/65/EC and 2011/61/EU) to Integrate Sustainability Risks
INSTITUTIONS: Institution(s): Financial Services and Markets Authority (FSMA)
DESCRIPTION: This Consultation Paper aims to fulfill the European Commission’s request for technical advice on potential amendments to delegated acts under European Directive 2009/65/EC (UCITS Directive) and Directive 2011/61/EU (AIFMD) with regard to the integration of sustainability risks and factors in the internal processes and procedures of UCITS management companies and alternative investment fund managers.

TITLE: Guideline on Environmental & Social Risk Management (ESRM) For Banks and Financial Institutions
DESCRIPTION: The ESRM guidelines set down standards for the identification, assessment, and management of E&S risks.

TITLE: Draft Amendment to Delegated Regulation 2017/565 Aims to Integrate Environmental, Social, and Governance (ESG) Considerations into Investment Advice and Portfolio Management
DESCRIPTION: In 2018, the European Commission drafted an amendment to the Delegated Regulation 2017/565 to integrate environmental, social, and governance (ESG) considerations and preferences into the investment advice and portfolio management provided by investment firms.

TITLE: Joint Statement in Support of a Sustainable Financial System for Australia and New Zealand
INSTITUTIONS: Institution(s): Investor Group on Climate Change, Principles for Responsible Investment, UNEP FI, Responsible Investment Association Australia
DESCRIPTION: The joint Statement in Support of a Sustainable Financial System for Australia and New Zealand is a set of recommendations across policy, regulation and finance practices that helps the finance sector contribute systematically to a more resilient sustainable economy.

TITLE: China Promotes Green Finance in Five Pilot Zones
DESCRIPTION: In 2017, China announced plans to set up pilot zones for green finance in Guangdong, Guizhou, Jiangxi, and Zhejiang provinces as well as the Xinjiang Uygur autonomous region.

TITLE: Seychelles’ Sovereign Blue Bond
DESCRIPTION: In October 2018, Republic of Seychelles issued a Blue Bond for an amount of USD15 million with a maturity of 10 years and interest payments (“coupons”) of 6.5%.

TITLE: Amendment to Regulation 2016/1011 Introduces a Framework for European Union (EU) Climate Transition and Paris-Aligned Benchmarks
DESCRIPTION: The European Union’s (EU) amendment to Regulation 2016/1011 (on indices used as benchmarks in financial instruments and financial contracts) introduces a regulatory framework that lays down minimum requirements for the EU Climate Transition Benchmark and EU Paris-aligned Benchmark.

TITLE: Council of Financial Regulators (CFR) Working Group on Financial Implications of Climate Change
INSTITUTIONS: Institution(s): Council of Financial Regulators (CFR) - comprising RBA, APRA, ASIC and the Australian Treasury
DESCRIPTION: The group provides a forum for APRA, the Australian Securities and Investment Commission (ASIC), the Reserve Bank of Australia (RBA) and the Australian Treasury to consider and coordinate actions to address the implications of the changing climate for the Australian financial system. The working group reports to the CFR, as needed, on international developments, emerging regulatory gaps and risks to the financial system in relation to climate change.

TITLE: Clarifying and Strengthening Trustees' Investment Duties
COUNTRY: Country: United Kingdom of Great Britain and Northern Ireland
DESCRIPTION: The Department for Work & Pensions proposed to require trustees to, by October 2019, where they are required to produce a Statement of Investment Principles, update or prepare it to set out: how they take account of financially material considerations, including (

TITLE: Guidelines on green, social and sustainable bonds
DESCRIPTION: The Moroccan Capital Market Authority (AMMC), with the support of the International Finance Corporation (IFC), issued their Green, Social and Sustainability Bond Guidelines.

TITLE: China Securities Regulatory Commission Green Bond Assessment Guidelines for Listed Companies
INSTITUTIONS: Institution(s): People's Bank of China and the China Securities Regulatory Commissions (CSRC)
DESCRIPTION: The China Securities Regulatory Commission has issued Green Bond Assessment Guidelines, which set out official requirements for what projects qualify as green, the management of proceeds, and reporting.

TITLE: The European Commission's Action Plan on Financing Sustainable Growth
DESCRIPTION: Implementation of the European Commission's (EC's) Action Plan on Sustainable Finance, which was adopted in March 2018, is underway, with support from an approved package of four legislative measures in May 2018 and adoption of a regulation on low-carbon benchmarks in March 2019.

TITLE: Belgium has Issued an EUR 4.5 Billion Green Bond
DESCRIPTION: In February 2018, Belgium issued an EUR 4.5 billion green bond, which is expected to grow to EUR 10 billion within four years.

TITLE: Policy brief “Green finance: the agenda for Russia”
INSTITUTIONS: Institution(s): The Ministry of Finance of the Russian federation and the Central Bank of Russia
DESCRIPTION: The Ministry of Finance of the Russian federation in November 2018 has published a policy brief on the green finance agenda for Russia prepared by the Working group on sustainable finance working in the framework of the Expert committee on the long-term investment market of the Central Bank of Russia.

TITLE: Bursa Malaysia Sustainability Reporting Guide
DESCRIPTION: The Sustainability Reporting Guide seeks to provide guidance on how to embed sustainability and help identify, evaluate and manage material EES risks and opportunities.

TITLE: Guide for Environmental and Social risk management
DESCRIPTION: On 22 November 2018, Paraguay’s Central Bank approved Resolution No. 8/2018 “Guide for the Management of Environmental Social Risks for Entities Regulated and Supervised by the Central Bank of Paraguay”, to be integrated within the credit risk analysis of financial institutions.

TITLE: Survey Finds Swedish Banks Have Made Progress on Sustainable Lending but Further Improvements are Needed
INSTITUTIONS: Institution(s): The Swedish Financial Supervisory Authority (Finansinspektionen)
DESCRIPTION: Finansinspektionen (FI), Sweden's financial supervisory authority, has conducted a survey of nine banks, which together account for the majority of total corporate lending in Sweden. This 2018 survey is a follow-up to the one that FI carried out in 2015 to note if any changes had been made in how the banks consider sustainability-related risks.

TITLE: Ontario Green Bank Regulation (Reg. 46/17: Ontario Climate Change Solutions Deployment Corporation)
DESCRIPTION: In 2017, the Ontario Ministry of the Environment and Climate Change (MOECC) filed the regulation that governs the Ontario Climate Change Solutions Deployment Corporation (OCCSDC), commonly referred to as the "Green Bank."

TITLE: The Government of the Republic of Lithuania issued a Sovereign Green Bond
INSTITUTIONS: Institution(s): Government of the Republic of Lithuania
DESCRIPTION: The Government of the Republic of Lithuania is the first public authority in the Baltic states to issue green bonds.

TITLE: California Senate Bill No. 964: climate-related financial risk
DESCRIPTION: California’s 2018 SB 964 requires the country’s two biggest pension funds to publicly disclose and analyze their climate-related investment risks.

TITLE: The City of Reykjavík Green Bond Framework
DESCRIPTION: The City of Reykjavík established a Green Bond Framework, under which eligible projects assist the City of Reykjavik in the transition to a low carbon economy. Projects included in the framework include:

TITLE: Mexico's Climate Change Law, and Amendments on a National Emissions Registry and Emissions Trading System
DESCRIPTION: Mexico’s Climate Change Law, which includes ambitious emissions reductions targets, was passed in 2012 and amended in 2014 to establish a National Emissions Registry and in 2018 to initiate a national emissions trading system.

TITLE: The California Climate Risk Carbon Initiative's Disclosure Requirement on Investments in Fossil Fuels
DESCRIPTION: The California Climate Risk Carbon Initiative's Disclosure Requirement requires all insurance companies with US$100 million in annual premiums doing business in California to disclose publicly their investments in coal, oil, gas, and utilities that rely on these fossil fuels.

TITLE: The National Stock Exchange of Costa Rica Launched Initiatives to Develop the Green Bond Market
DESCRIPTION: BNV has developed a number of initiatives to develop the green bond market

TITLE: Amman Stock Exchange Guidance on Sustainability Reporting
DESCRIPTION: In August 2018, Amman Stock Exchange issued guiding steps for the listed public shareholding companies on sustainability reporting.

TITLE: Sustainability Disclosure Guidelines
DESCRIPTION: The Sustainability Disclosure Guidelines provide a step by step approach on integrating sustainability in organisations, and detail indicators that should be considered when providing annual disclosure to The Exchange.

TITLE: Fiji has Issued a USD 50 Million Green Bond
INSTITUTIONS: Institution(s): Ministry of Economy and Reserve Bank of Fiji
DESCRIPTION: In October 2017, Fiji issued a USD 50 million green bond.

TITLE: Mexico's Green Bonds Principles
INSTITUTIONS: Institution(s): Consejo Consultivo de Finanzas Climáticas (Climate Finance Advisory Group)
DESCRIPTION: Mexico's Green Bonds Principles aim to establish common guidelines that can help green bond issuers in the Mexican market with the green bond issuance process as well as provide certainty to investors regarding the environmental benefits of the projects financed through the proceeds raised.

TITLE: Voluntary Guide for Creating Sustainability Reports
DESCRIPTION: The National Stock Exchange of Costa Rica has created a Sustainable Voluntary Guidance to help issuers in preparing and disclosing information about the ESG criteria.

TITLE: Guidance for listed companies on reporting ESG information to investors
DESCRIPTION: In 2018, Botswana Stock Exchange issued a guidance for BSE listed companies. The guidance is a voluntary tool and proposes five guiding principles for ESG reporting.

TITLE: Recommendation from the High Level Meeting on ESG Finance: Toward becoming a big power in ESG finance
INSTITUTIONS: Institution(s): High Level Meeting on ESG Finance
DESCRIPTION: In January 2018, the High Level Meeting on ESG Finance was set up for major players in the financial markets to gather under the initiative of the Minister of the Environment. In July 2018, the members of the High Level Meeting on ESG Finance released their recommendation called “Toward becoming a big power in ESG finance” aimed at bolstering ESG investment and enhancing climate-related disclosures.

TITLE: Investment Guidelines for Mexico's Retirement Funds Administrators
DESCRIPTION: Mexico has revised recommendations that form the regulatory backbone of the Afores (Mexico’s Retirement Funds Administrators) system, which include environmental, social, and governance (ESG) factors in the Afores' investment analysis procedures.

TITLE: Vienna Stock Exchange’s Green and Social Bonds Platform
DESCRIPTION: The Vienna Stock Exchange launched a platform for ‘green’ securities for Austrian and international issuers.

TITLE: Solactive oekom ESG Fossil Free Eurozone 50 Index
INSTITUTIONS: Institution(s): The Federal State of Berlin, Oekom Research and Solactive
DESCRIPTION: Solactive oekom ESG Fossil Free Eurozone 50 Index, which is customized to the State of Berlin’s divesting policies on reserve funds, aims to achieve the goals of the UN Global Compact as well as allocate funds to environmental, social, and governance (ESG) investment objectives, while ensuring the ease of tradability of the index constituents.

TITLE: Maldives Green Fund
DESCRIPTION: In December 2018, the Republic of Maldives established a green fund to manage revenue sourced form green taxes.

TITLE: Australian Asset Owner Stewardship Code
INSTITUTIONS: Institution(s): Australian Council of Superannuation Investors (ACSI)
DESCRIPTION: The Australian Asset Owner Stewardship Code (Code) aims to increase the transparency and accountability of stewardship activities in Australia.

TITLE: Climate Finance Facility
DESCRIPTION: The Development Bank of Southern Africa (DBSA) is an infrastructure development finance institution (DFI) that supports financing of infrastructure in the energy, water, transport and ICT sectors in sub-Saharan Africa.

TITLE: National Policy on Climate Finance
INSTITUTIONS: Institution(s): National Treasury of the Republic of Kenya
DESCRIPTION: The National Policy on Climate Finance provides legal National Policy and institutional frameworks for guiding and promoting climate finance flows in Kenya and reporting climate finance through budget tracking.

TITLE: Germany's State of North-Rhine Westphalia has Issued Three Sustainability Bonds
INSTITUTIONS: Institution(s): The State of North-Rhine Westphalia
DESCRIPTION: Germany's State of North-Rhine Westphalia has issued three sustainability bonds.

TITLE: Corporate Governance Guide for Banks
DESCRIPTION: The Corporate Governance Guide’s purpose is the promotion and implementation of best practices in governance and sustainability within the banking sector.

TITLE: General Resolution No. 764/2018 - Annex I "Argentina Guidelines for the Offering of Green Social and Sustainable Bonds" and Resolution 788/2019
INSTITUTIONS: Institution(s): Comisión Nacional de Valores (the Argentine Securities and Exchange Commission)
DESCRIPTION: Argentina's Guidelines on Green, Social, and Sustainable Bonds introduce the conceptual framework for the financing of projects that generate environmental and social impact.

TITLE: Germany's Renewable Energy Act (Erneuerbare-Energien-Gesetz)
DESCRIPTION: The purpose of the German Renewable Energy Act is to enable the energy supply to develop in a sustainable manner and to support climate change mitigation and environmental protection.

TITLE: Disclosure Requirements for Issuance and Listing of Green Debt Securities (CIR/IMD/DF/51/2017)
INSTITUTIONS: Institution(s): The Securities and Exchange Board of India
DESCRIPTION: India issued a Circular on Disclosure Requirements for Issuance and Listing of Green Debt Securities (CIR/IMD/DF/51/2017) in May 2017. It includes a list of project and asset categories that fall under "green" debt securities, and requires issuers of green debt securities to make certain disclosures.

TITLE: Indonesia's Clean Energy Handbook for Financial Service Institutions
INSTITUTIONS: Institution(s): Financial Services Authority of Indonesia (OJK)
DESCRIPTION: Indonesia's Clean Energy Handbook for Financial Service Institutions includes lending manuals for five types of renewable energy investments—mini hydro, biogas, biomass, photovoltaic, and wind.

TITLE: Pilot tests to analyse the climate alignment of financial portfolios
INSTITUTIONS: Institution(s): The Federal Office for the Environment (FOEN) and the State Secretariat for International Financial Matters (SIF)
DESCRIPTION: Switzerland's Federal Office for the Environment (FOEN) and the State Secretariat for International Financial Matters (SIF) initiated pilot tests to analyse the climate alignment of financial portfolios in 2017.

TITLE: Chile's National Action Plan on Business and Human Rights
DESCRIPTION: Chile's National Action Plan on Business and Human Rights identifies gaps within the national corporate social responsibility (CSR) strategy as well as the means to fill these gaps.

TITLE: Green Bond Framework
INSTITUTIONS: Institution(s): The Federal Ministry of Environment of the Republic of Nigeria in partnership with the Federal Ministry of Finance
DESCRIPTION: The Green Bond Framework provides details on eligible project categories, the project evaluation and selection process, how proceeds will be managed, and how the government intends to report on projects on an ongoing basis.

TITLE: French Strategy for Green Finance
DESCRIPTION: France's Ministry of the Ecological and Solidarity Transition and Ministry of Economy and Finance commissioned a French Strategy for Green Finance.

TITLE: Legislative Decree No. 32/2007 and Article 2428 of the Italian Civil Code Require Reporting on Non-Financial Indicators
DESCRIPTION: Legislative Decree No. 32/2007 and Article 2428 of the Italian Civil Code states that director's reports should include financial and non-financial key performance indicators relevant to the specific business of the company, including information relating to environmental and employee matters.

TITLE: Mexico’s Catastrophe Bonds Provide Financial Protection Against Losses From Covered Natural Disasters
DESCRIPTION: Mexico issued the world’s first sovereign catastrophe bond in 2006, followed by additional catastrophe bonds issued in 2009, 2012 and 2017, in order to provide Mexico with financial protection against losses from covered natural disasters such as earthquakes and tropical cyclones.

TITLE: Vanuatu Climate Finance Roadmap
INSTITUTIONS: Institution(s): National Advisory Board on Climate Change & Disaster Risk Reduction
DESCRIPTION: The purpose of the roadmap is to better guide the Government in mobilising climate finance to address national priorities.

TITLE: Green Banking Guidelines
DESCRIPTION: The Green Banking Guidelines cover Environmental and Social Risk in lending, financing green projects and reducing the banks’ carbon footprint.

TITLE: France Requires Companies to include Environmental and Social Issues in Non-Financial Declarations (Order No. 2017-1180 and Decree No. 2017-1265)
DESCRIPTION: In France, companies with more than 500 employees with a balance sheet total exceeding 20 million euros or with a turnover of more than 40 million need to provide a "declaration of extra-financial performance of companies." This declaration must include specific environmental and social information, including on climate change, according to Order No. 2017-1180 and Decree No. 2017-1265.

TITLE: Morocco's Framework Partnership Agreement Aims to Promote Investments in the Environment and Sustainable Development
INSTITUTIONS: Institution(s): Autorite de Controle des Assurances et de la Prevoyance (ACAPS)
DESCRIPTION: In 2017, a Framework Partnership Agreement was signed between Morocco's Ministry of Energy, Mines and Sustainable Development, the Supervisory Authority of Insurance and Social Welfare, and the Moroccan Federation of Insurance and Reinsurance Companies in order to promote investments in the environment and sustainable development and to meet targets for sustainable investments by Moroccan insurance companies set out in the National Roadmap.

TITLE: South Africa Sustainable Finance Initiative
INSTITUTIONS: Institution(s): National Treasury and market institutions
DESCRIPTION: South Africa's Sustainable Finance Initiative aims to: (i) define sustainable finance for a South African context; (ii) incorporate perspectives from all parts of the financial sector; (iii) describe the global and national drivers for sustainable finance, as well as existing industry initiatives; (iv) map supply and demand for, as well as barriers to, sustainable finance; and (v) provide recommendations on a national strategic approach and the role of regulatory agencies and industry stakeholders.

TITLE: First Green Bond issuance on the Moroccan Market
INSTITUTIONS: Institution(s): Moroccan Agency for Sustainable Energy (MASEN)
DESCRIPTION: Moroccan Agency of Sustainable Energy S.A. (MASEN), a state owned public limited company, issued Morocco’s first green bond in November 2016 amounted at 1.15 billion Dirham (USD 117mn).

TITLE: Cambodia's National Environment Strategy and Action Plan (NESAP) 2016-2023
INSTITUTIONS: Institution(s): National Council for Sustainable Development (NCSD) of Cambodia
DESCRIPTION: In December 2017, the Ministry of Environment and the National Council for Sustainable Development (NCSD) of the Kingdom of Cambodia released National Environment Strategy and Action Plan (NESAP) 2016-2023.

TITLE: France has Issued an EUR 7.5 Billion Green Bond
INSTITUTIONS: Institution(s): Directorate General of the Treasury
DESCRIPTION: In January 2017, the French Government issued an EUR 7.5 billion green bond. Proceeds will be allocated to projects that target climate change mitigation, biodiversity protection, climate change adaptation, and pollution control.

TITLE: Assessment of Climate-Related Risks for the Dutch Financial Sector
DESCRIPTION: In 2017, the central bank of the Netherlands—De Nederlandsche Bank (DNB)—published an assessment of climate-related risks that are relevant to the Dutch financial sector, along with the consequences of these risks for supervisory authorities, financial institutions, and policymakers.

TITLE: Issuance of Green Sukuk in Malaysia
DESCRIPTION: Malaysia has pioneered the issuance of Green SRI Sukuk since the introduction of the SRI sukuk framework.

TITLE: Framework of the Guyana Green State Development Strategy and Financing Mechanisms
DESCRIPTION: In March 2017, the Ministry of the Presidency of Guyana issued the Green State Development Strategy (GSDS) with the timeframe of next 15 year.

TITLE: Investment Governance Code for Institutional Investors
DESCRIPTION: The SEC has launched the Investment Governance Code (I Code) as a guideline for responsible and sustainable investment management of institutional investors.

TITLE: Île-de-France has Issued EUR 2.7 Billion Through Green and Sustainability Bonds Between 2012 and 2017
DESCRIPTION: The Ile-de-France Region—a frequent and regular issuer in the green bond market—has issued EUR 2.7 billion through green and sustainability bonds between 2012 and 2017.

TITLE: Nigeria has Issued a USD 29.7 Million Green Bond
INSTITUTIONS: Institution(s): Ministry of Finance and Ministry of Environment
DESCRIPTION: In December 2017, Nigeria issued a USD 29.7 million green bond, which commits to the deployment of federal funds for new projects that help Nigeria to meet its climate commitments and start diversifying its economy from oil-based revenues.

TITLE: A Guide on Sustainability Reporting in Chile
INSTITUTIONS: Institution(s): Bolsa de Comercio de Santiago
DESCRIPTION: This Guide on Sustainability Reporting in Chile aims to help issuers prepare and publish information related to environmental, social, and governance (ESG) matters.

TITLE: Stewardship Code for Institutional Investors
DESCRIPTION: The purpose of the Stewardship Code is to encourage the institutional investment community to take action to serve as responsible stewards for their beneficiaries and to help to promote good corporate governance and the sustainable success of listed companies (issuers) in the capital markets.

TITLE: Italy's National Energy Strategy 2017
DESCRIPTION: Italy's National Energy Strategy (SEN) is a ten–year plan that aims to anticipate and manage the long-term change of the national energy system. The Strategy lays the foundation for the construction of an advanced and innovative energy model, with the objectives of making the national energy system more competitive, more sustainable, and more secure.

TITLE: Evaluating Climate Change Risks in the Banking Sector
INSTITUTIONS: Institution(s): Directorate General of the Treasury (with support from the Banque de France and the Prudential Supervisory and Resolution Authority)
DESCRIPTION: In 2017, France's Directorate General of the Treasury published a report on climate-related risks in the banking sector.

TITLE: Japan's Guidebook on Environmental, Social, and Governance (ESG) Investment
INSTITUTIONS: Institution(s): Government of Japan, Ministry of the Environment, Japan (MOEJ)
DESCRIPTION: Japan's Guidebook on Environmental, Social, and Governance (ESG) Investment aims to provide a basic understanding of ESG investing and trends.

TITLE: The Brazil Innovation Lab for Climate Finance
INSTITUTIONS: Institution(s): Brazilian Securities and Exchange Commission (CVM) and the Brazilian Development Association, Inter-American Development Bank
DESCRIPTION: The Global Innovation Lab for Climate Finance (the Lab) is a local network of public and private investors and leaders that identify, develop, and launch transformative investment solutions that can drive funds for Brazil’s national climate priorities.

TITLE: Latvian state-owned development finance institution issued a green bond
DESCRIPTION: In October 207, state owned development finance institution Altum issued a green bond in the total value of EUR 20 million with a maturity date of 17 October 2024.

TITLE: Listing Rules for the Kazakhstan Stock Exchange Require Disclosure of Environmental and Social Information
DESCRIPTION: The Kazakhstan Stock Exchange's Listing Rules require companies to disclose information in their annual reports on their social and environmental liability and responsibility.

TITLE: Thailand's Corporate Governance Code Requires Sustainability Reporting
INSTITUTIONS: Institution(s): Securities and Exchange Commission of Thailand
DESCRIPTION: In 2017, Thailand's Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) issued a new Corporate Governance Code, which replaced the 2012 Principles of Good Corporate Governance for listed companies issued by the Stock Exchange of Thailand (SET).

TITLE: The EU Circular Economy Finance Support Platform
DESCRIPTION: The Circular Economy Finance Support Platform is a web tool that continuously showcases new examples of innovative ways in which industry, small- and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs), and other business add to the circular economy in Europe.

TITLE: China's Guidelines for Establishing the Green Financial System
INSTITUTIONS: Institution(s): People’s Bank of China (PBoC), Ministry of Finance, National Development and Reform Commission (NDRC), Ministry of Environmental Protection, China Banking Regulatory Commission (CBRC), China Securities Regulatory Commission (CSRC) and China Insurance Regulatory Commission (CIRC)
DESCRIPTION: China's Guidelines for Establishing the Green Financial System aim to mobilise and incentivise more capital to invest in green sectors, while restricting investment in polluting sectors.

TITLE: Stocktake and Review of Sustainable Finance Opportunities for Argentina
DESCRIPTION: This stocktaking report of sustainable finance opportunities in Argentina identifies system-wide needs, barriers to scaling up, and priority actions on how the country’s financial system can unlock investment and contribute to the SDGs and the Paris Agreement on climate change.

TITLE: Bali Center for Sustainable Finance to Support Sustainable Development Program
INSTITUTIONS: Institution(s): Financial Services Authority of Indonesia (OJK)
DESCRIPTION: The Bali Center for Sustainable Finance (BCSF) was set up to provide a study and learning center about sustainable finance for financial services professionals, policy makers, business executives, and the general public.

TITLE: Sustainability and Diversity Improvement Act 257/ME (Nachhaltigkeits- und Diversitätsverbesserungsgesetz)
DESCRIPTION: The Austrian Sustainability and Diversity Improvement Act (Nachhaltigkeits- und Diversitätsverbesserungsgesetz; NaDiVeG) implements EU Directive 2014/95/EU and amended the Austrian Commercial Code (the Unternehmensgesetzbuch, UGB) with sections 243b and 267a.

TITLE: Green Bond Guidelines Issued by China's National Development and Reform Commission (NDRC)
INSTITUTIONS: Institution(s): National Development and Reform Commission
DESCRIPTION: China's National Development and Reform Commission (NDRC) has issued Guidelines on the Issuance of Green Bonds.

TITLE: Internal Governance and Asset Stewardship Standard (No. 23)
DESCRIPTION: The Australian Financial Services Council's (FSC) Standard No. 23—Principles of Internal Governance and Asset Stewardship—promotes the adoption of high standards that are consistent with other leading capital markets.

TITLE: The European Union’s Shareholder Rights Directive II Aims to Encourage Long-term Engagement Between Companies and Shareholders
DESCRIPTION: The Shareholder Rights Directive II (SRD II) aims to increase transparency in the investment chain and sets out a framework for better, more long-term engagement between companies and their shareholders in the European Union (EU).

TITLE: Indonesia's Regulation on the Application of Sustainable Finance (No. 51/POJK.03/2017)
INSTITUTIONS: Institution(s): Financial Services Authority of Indonesia (OJK)
DESCRIPTION: Indonesia's Regulation on the Application of Sustainable Finance (No. 51/POJK.03/2017) requires financial services agencies, issuers, and public companies to provide the funding sources needed for achieving sustainable development goals and ensuring adequate financing for efforts to address climate change.

TITLE: Croatian Accounting Act
DESCRIPTION: The Croatian Accounting Act implements EU Directive 2014/95/EU and requires large undertakings registering 500 and more employees to disclose non-financial information in any of the forms of non-financial disclosures.

TITLE: The Ontario Pension Benefits Act Requires Environmental Disclosures
INSTITUTIONS: Institution(s): Financial Services Commission of Ontario
DESCRIPTION: The Ontario Pension Benefits Act requires pension funds in Ontario to disclose whether environmental factors are incorporated into their statement of investment policies and procedures.

TITLE: Environmental and Social Risk Management (ESRM) Guidelines
DESCRIPTION: Building on its Environmental Risk Management Guidelines introduced in 2011, Bangladesh Bank issued updated Environmental and Social Risk Management (ESRM) Guidelines for banks and financial institutions in Bangladesh in 2017.

TITLE: Collaborative Initiative for Green Finance in Singapore
INSTITUTIONS: Institution(s): Singapore Institute of International Affairs, Inquiry into the Design of a Sustainable Financial System (UN Environment Inquiry)
DESCRIPTION: The Singapore Institute of International Affairs started the “Collaborative Initiative for Green Finance in Singapore” in 2017 in partnership with the UN Environment Inquiry, with the support of the Monetary Authority of Singapore (MAS).

TITLE: Indonesia's Regulation on the Issuance and the Terms of Green Bond (No. 60/POJK.04/2017) Sets Standards for Green Bond Issuance
INSTITUTIONS: Institution(s): Financial Services Authority of Indonesia (OJK)
DESCRIPTION: Indonesia's Regulation on the Issuance and the Terms of Green Bond (No. 60/POJK.04/2017) sets standards for green bond issuance.

TITLE: Companies Number 3 Law of 2017
DESCRIPTION: The Companies Number 3 Law of 2017 implements EU Directive 2014/95/EU and requires public interest entities with an average number of employees exceeding 500 and which also have a total balance sheet of more than EUR 20 million or a net turnover of more than EUR 40 million, or both to disclose non-financial and diversity information.

TITLE: Canada's Pension Plan Governance Guidelines
INSTITUTIONS: Institution(s): Canadian Association of Pension Supervisory Authorities
DESCRIPTION: The Canadian Association of Pension Supervisory Authorities (CAPSA) has amended its guidance in February 2017, to list environmental, social, and governarnce (ESG) issues as typical risks to be evaluated by pension trustees.

TITLE: The Australian Prudential Regulation Authority (APRA) Calls on Financial Sector Entities to Include Climate Change in Internal Risk Management Processes
DESCRIPTION: At the 2017 Insurance Council of Australia Annual Forum, Geoff Summerhayes, Executive Board Member at the Australian Prudential Regulation Authority (APRA), said that climate change should no longer be seen as merely a "future problem or a non-financial problem," and discussed both the physical risks and transition risks of climate change.

TITLE: Singapore's Sustainable Bond Grant Scheme
DESCRIPTION: The Monetary Authority of Singapore (MAS) launched a Sustainable Bond Grant scheme in 2017 that encourages the issuance of green, social and sustainability bonds in Singapore by helping issuers to cover additional costs associated with external reviews.

TITLE: Act No. 563/1991 Coll. on accounting
DESCRIPTION: Act No. 563/1991 Coll. on accounting implements EU Directive 2014/95/EU and requires companies and parent companies of large groups that are public-interest entities and, at the same time, employ on average more than 500 employees in the course of an accounting period, to publish information in their annual reports regarding environmental, social and employee issues, respect for human rights and the fight against corruption and bribery.

TITLE: Working Paper on the Potential Impacts of Climate Change on Central Banks' Monetary and Financial Stability Objectives
COUNTRY: Country: United Kingdom of Great Britain and Northern Ireland
DESCRIPTION: "Let’s talk about the weather: The impact of climate change on central banks" is a working paper published by the Bank of England that examines channels via which climate change and policies to mitigate it could affect a central bank’s ability to meet its monetary and financial stability objectives.

TITLE: The Netherland's Sustainable Finance Platform
DESCRIPTION: De Nederlandsche Bank (DNB) established the Sustainable Finance Platform in 2016 to promote and increase awareness of sustainable funding in the financial sector, with a particular focus on environmental, social, and governance (ESG) aspects.

TITLE: Kazakhstan is Developing a Green Finance Regulatory Framework, Covering Green Bonds, Loans, Technologies, and Projects
INSTITUTIONS: Institution(s): Astana International Financial Centre (AIFC) and the EBRD
DESCRIPTION: In August 2019, the Astana International Financial Centre (AIFC) adopted the Concept of a Green Financial System for Kazakhstan, the AIFC implementation strategy, and a set the rules for issuing green bonds in the Astana International Exchange (AIX). In September 2019, AIFC announced that it is working to create a regulatory framework for green finance, which is anticipated to cover green finance instruments such as green bonds, loans, technologies, and projects.

TITLE: Disaster Risk Financing in the Third Northern Uganda Social Action Fund
DESCRIPTION: The Third Northern Uganda Social Action Fund project, financed by the World Bank, includes a Disaster Risk Financing (DRF) sub-component that aims to develop a mechanism for scaling up assistance to poor and vulnerable households immediately following disaster events and a system to cover the costs of this expansion.

TITLE: Sustainable Banking Protocol
INSTITUTIONS: Institution(s): Ecuadorian Association of Private Banks (ASOBANCA)
DESCRIPTION: In November 2016, Asociación de Bancos Privados del Ecuador (ASOBANCA), launched the "Sustainable Banking Protocol" with 10 signatory banks that represent more than 80% of the market share and with the participation and support of IFC/SBN.

TITLE: Green Finance Initiative
COUNTRY: Country: United Kingdom of Great Britain and Northern Ireland
DESCRIPTION: The Green Finance Initiative (GFI) was launched in 2016 by the City of London Corporation and the UK government to improve the financing options for sustainable infrastructure projects and make London a world leader in green finance.

TITLE: Guidelines for Observation and Exclusion from the Government Pension Fund Global (as Amended in 2016)
DESCRIPTION: In December 2014, Norway adopted Guidelines for Observation and Exclusion from the Government Pension Fund Global, and subsequently amended them in December 2015 and February 2016.

TITLE: Environmental, Social, and Governance (ESG) Reporting Guide—An Appendix to the Rules Governing the Listing of Securities on the Stock Exchange of Hong Kong
DESCRIPTION: The Rules Governing the Listing of Securities on the Stock Exchange of Hong Kong includes an appendix with an Environmental, Social, and Governance (ESG) Reporting Guide.

TITLE: Circular on Lending Transactions of Credit Institutions and/or Foreign Bank Branches with Customers (Circular 39/2016/TT-NHNN)
DESCRIPTION: Vietnam's Circular 39 contains principles relevant to Environmental, Social, and Governance (ESG) factors, including one that requires lending transactions between a credit institution and a customer be performed in conformity with all regulations and legislation on environmental protection.

TITLE: Singapore Stewardship Principles for Responsible Investors
DESCRIPTION: The Singapore Stewardship Principles (SSP) for Responsible Investors are intended to enhance a positive investment environment by encouraging companies to pursue the spirit of good governance and stewardship, with the ultimate objective of helping companies secure their performance over the long term.

TITLE: Survey of Environmental Practices of Brazilian Insurance Companies
DESCRIPTION: Brazil's Superintendence of Private Insurance (Superintendencia de Seguros Privados, or SUSEP) conducted a survey in 2016 to obtain data and information about market practice on sustainability issues, with a focus on climate change.

TITLE: High Level Expert Group on Sustainable Finance
DESCRIPTION: The European Commission (EC) established a High-Level Expert Group (HLEG) on Sustainable Finance in December 2016.
