TITLE: Italian National Dialogue on Sustainable Finance
INSTITUTIONS: Institution(s): Ministry of Environment & UNEP Inquiry
DESCRIPTION: Italy's National Dialogue on Sustainable Finance was established to identify options that would improve the integration of sustainability factors across the country's financial sector.

TITLE: King IV Code on Corporate Governance in South Africa
INSTITUTIONS: Institution(s): Institute of Directors in Southern Africa (IoDSA)
DESCRIPTION: The King IV Code on Corporate Governance for South Africa was updated in 2016 to align South Africa’s corporate governance regime with the OECD's principles of corporate governance, including on corporate environmental and social impacts from their activities.

TITLE: Korea Stewardship Code
DESCRIPTION: The Korea Stewardship Code, the “Principles on the Stewardship Responsibilities of Institutional Investors”, sets forth seven detailed principles and guidelines that institutional investors holding the shares of publicly listed companies in Korea should follow to fulfill their fiduciary duties as

TITLE: Egypt's Corporate Governance Code
DESCRIPTION: Egypt's Corporate Governance Code serves as a guide for best practices in the fields of governance, transparency, and prudent management for all stakeholders of the companies adopting the Code.

TITLE: Too Late, Too Sudden: The Impact of a Low-Carbon Transition on Systemic Risk
INSTITUTIONS: Institution(s): European Systemic Risk Board (ESRB) Advisory Scientific Committee
DESCRIPTION: This report highlights that making the transition to a low-carbon economy too late risks affecting the economy of the European Union.

TITLE: Green Finance Task Force - Green Finance Hub Report
DESCRIPTION: The Green Finance Hub Report sets out eight recommendations for Hong Kong to become a regional green finance hub.

TITLE: Bangladesh Sets Green Finance Minimum Target at 5% for Banks and Financial Institutions
DESCRIPTION: To expedite the ongoing sustainability and climate change initiatives of banks and financial institutions (FIs), Bangladesh Bank set a minimum target of direct green finance at five percent of the total loan disbursement / investment from January 2016 onwards for all banks and FIs (GBCSRD Circular No.04/2014).

TITLE: Code 13: Governance and administration of occupational trust-based schemes providing money purchase benefits
COUNTRY: Country: United Kingdom of Great Britain and Northern Ireland
DESCRIPTION: This Guidance sets out on how trustees should consider taking into account the ESG and ethical factors that may be financially significant to their investment risk assessment, both for short and longer term.

TITLE: The Finnish Accounting Act, as Amended in 2016, Requires Large Public Interest Entities to Report on Non-Financial Issues
DESCRIPTION: The Finnish Accounting Act (1336/1997), as amended in 2016 by Act 2016/1376, requires large public interest entities to include material non-financial issues in their annual/financial reports from financial year 2017 onwards. This includes information on environmental matters, social and employee-related matters, respect for human rights, anti-corruption, and bribery.

TITLE: Public Consultation on Long-Term and Sustainable Investments
DESCRIPTION: The objective of the European Commission's public consultation on long-term and sustainable investments is to gather information on how institutional investors, asset managers, and other service providers factor environmental, social, and governance (ESG) information and performance of companies or assets into investment decisions.

TITLE: Principles of Responsible Ownership
INSTITUTIONS: Institution(s): The Securities and Futures Commission (SFC)
DESCRIPTION: Hong Kong's Securities and Futures Commission (SFC) has developed non-binding, voluntary Principles of Responsible Ownership to guide and assist investors in determining how best to meet their ownership responsibilities.

TITLE: Cambodian Sustainable Finance Initiative
INSTITUTIONS: Institution(s): The Association of Banks in Cambodia (ABC), the National Bank of Cambodia and the Ministry of Environment
DESCRIPTION: In September 2016, Cambodia launched the Sustainable Finance Initiative, which aims to establish best practices and educate its members on sustainable banking practices.

TITLE: 2016 Appropriation Directions
INSTITUTIONS: Institution(s): The Swedish Financial Supervisory Authority (Finansinspektionen)
DESCRIPTION: In the 2016 appropriation directions, Sweden's FI has been commissioned to identify and investigate the possibilities of the authority to contribute to sustainable development. These appropriation directions set out the objectives of the agencies' activities and how much money they have available

TITLE: Climate Change and Financial Markets Report
DESCRIPTION: Germany's Ministry of Finance published a report in 2016 on the potential impact of climate change on its financial market stability.

TITLE: Luxembourg - European Investment Bank (EIB) Climate Finance Platform
INSTITUTIONS: Institution(s): The Grand Duchy of Luxembourg and the European Investment Bank (EIB)
DESCRIPTION: The Luxembourg - European Investment Bank (EIB) Climate Finance Platform aims to fund high-impact climate action projects and help attract additional private finance to climate-related projects.

TITLE: Victoria, Australia has Issued a USD 225 Million Green Bond
DESCRIPTION: In July 2016, Victoria, Australia, issued a USD 225 million green bond.

TITLE: Mongolia's Green Development Policy and Action Plan
INSTITUTIONS: Institution(s): Ministry of Environment and Green Development
DESCRIPTION: Mongolia's Green Development Policy and associated Action Plan, together, aim to introduce and implement principles of sustainable financing into the country's banking and financial systems.

TITLE: The Russian Export Center JSC follows the OECD Recommendation of the Council on Common Approaches for Officially Supported Export Credits and Environmental and Social Due Diligence
DESCRIPTION: Following best practices and international experience of environmental and social risk management, the REC Group follows the OECD Recommendation of the Council on Common Approaches for Officially Supported Export Credits and Environmental and Social Due Diligence (Common Approaches).

TITLE: Amendment to the German Commercial Code (Section 289b) Requires Companies to Include Non-Financial Information on Corporate Social Responsibility (CSR) in their Reporting
DESCRIPTION: In 2016, an amendment to the German Commercial Code (Section 289b) was approved; it requires major capital market-oriented companies with an average of more than 500 employees to include non-financial information on corporate social responsibility (CSR) in their status reports.

TITLE: European Union Directive (2016/2341) Requires Institutions for Occupational Retirement Provision (IORPs) to Take Environmental, Social, and Governance (ESG) Factors into Account
DESCRIPTION: The European Union (EU) Directive 2016/2341 requires Institutions for Occupational Retirement Provision (IORPs) to take environmental, social, and governance (ESG) factors into account in their risk management systems.

TITLE: Guidance on ESG reporting
DESCRIPTION: In December 2016, Qatar Stock Exchange published its Guidance on ESG Reporting to assist listed companies wishing to incorporate ESG reporting into their existing reporting processes.

TITLE: Morocco has Established a Scheme to Cover the Consequences of Catastrophic Events (Law No. 110-14)
DESCRIPTION: In August 2016, Morocco adopted a new disaster risk insurance law (No. 110-14), which amends the law relating to the insurance code (No. 17-99).

TITLE: Corporate Governance Regulation
INSTITUTIONS: Institution(s): National Supervisory Board of the Financial System (Conassif)
DESCRIPTION: The National Supervisory Board of the Financial System (Conassif) issued a set of regulations laying down the international standards and principles that should be incorporated into the corporate governance strategies of the entities it supervises.

TITLE: Review of Russia's Financial Market Regulation, Including Provisions on Green Bonds
DESCRIPTION: Russia's Central Bank conducted a review of its financial market regulation, which includes analyses on green banking and green bonds.

TITLE: France's Socially Responsible Investment (SRI) Label
DESCRIPTION: France's Socially Responsible Investment (SRI) Label is a tool for choosing sustainable and responsible investments.

TITLE: Legal Guide to Do Business in Colombia
DESCRIPTION: This is a guide for investors interested in Colombia, which includes a recommendation for companies to include corporate social responsibility (CSR) policies in line with the Global Reporting Initiative's (GRI) framework for sustainability reporting.

TITLE: Morocco's National Catastrophe Risk Insurance Program
INSTITUTIONS: Institution(s): World Bank, Development Partners and Moroccan Government
DESCRIPTION: Morocco's National Catastrophe Risk Insurance Program will cover risks ranging from floods, droughts, tsunamis, landslides, and earthquakes.

TITLE: Greek Law 4403/2016 on the Publication of Non-Financial Information
DESCRIPTION: Greek Law n. 4403/2016 incorporated into the Greek legal system the EU Directive 2013/34/EC and relates to the obligation, for large SA companies qualifying as public interest entities as per Annex A of the Law, to prepare Administrative Report and Non-Financial Statement

TITLE: Assessment of Climate Change and Financial Stability
INSTITUTIONS: Institution(s): The Swedish Financial Supervisory Authority (Finansinspektionen)
DESCRIPTION: This report analyses how climate change may affect financial stability in the long run, and which measures may be needed to dampen its negative effects on the financial system.

TITLE: Energy Transition for Green Growth Law (No. 2015-992) Requires Climate-Related Financial Disclosures
DESCRIPTION: France's Energy Transition for Green Growth Law (No. 2015-992, relative à la transition énergétique pour la croissance verte) sets out climate-related financial disclosure requirements for listed companies, bank and credit providers, and institutional investors.

TITLE: Notice (No. 39) on the Issue of Green Financial Bonds in China’s Inter-Bank Bond Market
DESCRIPTION: The People’s Bank of China published a Notice (No. 39) in December 2015 on the issue of green financial bonds in the inter-bank bond market.

TITLE: Dutch Corporate Governance Code Includes Provisions on Corporate Social Responsibility (CSR)
DESCRIPTION: The Dutch Corporate Governance Code contains principles and best practice provisions that regulate relations between the management board, supervisory board, and shareholders, including provisions on the treatment of corporate social responsibility (CSR) activities.

TITLE: EUR 750 Million Sovereign Green Bond Issued by Poland
DESCRIPTION: In 2016, Poland issued a EUR 750 million sovereign green bond.

TITLE: Climate Change Fund under the Climate Change Act 2016
DESCRIPTION: The Act provides a regulatory framework for an enhanced response to climate change and provides mechanisms for establishing effective institutional arrangements for climate action including climate financing.

TITLE: Southeast Europe and Central Asia (SEECA) Catastrophe Risk Insurance Facility
INSTITUTIONS: Institution(s): Government of Kazakhstan, World Bank, Industry Partners
DESCRIPTION: The development objective of the Southeast Europe and Central Asia (SEECA) Catastrophe Risk Insurance Facility (CRIF) Project is to assist Kazakhstan in developing a modern catastrophe insurance market infrastructure that will support the launch of affordable, innovative catastrophe insurance products covering the risks of weather extremes.

TITLE: China's 13th Five Year Plan (2016-2020) Includes Recommendations from the Green Finance Task Force
DESCRIPTION: In 2015, China approved its 13th Five-Year Plan (2016-2020), which includes recommendations from the Green Finance Task Force (GFTF) that was established by the State Council in 2014.

TITLE: Time for Transition: An Exploratory Study of the Transition to a Carbon-Neutral Economy
DESCRIPTION: The Netherland's central bank—De Nederlandsche Bank (DNB)—has published an exploratory study on the transition to a carbon-neutral economy.

TITLE: Green Bond Guidelines
DESCRIPTION: The Federal Ministry of Environment issued Green Bond Guidelines to guide the process for issuance of green bonds targeted at the Nigeria market.

TITLE: Australia's Environmental, Social, and Governance (ESG) Reporting Guide
INSTITUTIONS: Institution(s): Australian Financial Services Council (FSC), Australian Council of Superannuation Investors (ACSI)
DESCRIPTION: In 2015, the Australian Council of Superannuation Investors (ACSI) and Financial Services Council (FSC) published an Environmental, Social, and Governance (ESG) Reporting Guide, which aims to assist companies in disclosing their ESG risks in a consistent and comparable manner that is useful for investors.

TITLE: The Environmental Protection Law of the People's Republic of China
INSTITUTIONS: Institution(s): Ministry of Ecology and Environment
DESCRIPTION: The Environmental Protection Law of the People's Republic of China summarizes the existing regulation on disclosure and requests companies to report data about pollution to increase transparency.

TITLE: Expert Group on Green Transition and Competitiveness
DESCRIPTION: Sweden's Expert Group on Green Transition and Competitiveness promotes investments in sustainable development and investigates ways of achieving the changes Sweden needs to become an ecologically sustainable society with a competitive business sector. The group will analyse issues including sustainable investment, economic incentives, systems solutions for resource efficiency, research and skills development, and impact on business.

TITLE: The California Lending for Energy and Environmental Needs (CLEEN) Center
DESCRIPTION: The California Lending for Energy and Environmental Needs (CLEEN) Center provides direct public financing to municipalities, universities, schools, and hospitals to help meet the State's goals for greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions reduction, water conservation, and environmental conservation.

TITLE: The Corporate Governance Code of Italian Listed Companies (Legislative 254/2016)
DESCRIPTION: The Italian Corporate Governance Code as amended requires large companies (listed companies, banks, and insurance companies) to make disclosures on non-financial matters such as environmental, social, and employee-related matters, anti-corruption and bribery issues, respect for human rights and diversity.

TITLE: FTSE4Good Bursa Malaysia Index
DESCRIPTION: In December 2014, Bursa Malaysia and FTSE launched an Environmental, Social and Governance (ESG) index i.e. FTSE4Good Bursa Malaysia Index for the Malaysian market.

TITLE: The Impact of Climate Change on the UK Insurance Sector
COUNTRY: Country: United Kingdom of Great Britain and Northern Ireland
DESCRIPTION: In 2015, the United Kingdom's Prudential Regulation Authority (PRA) published a report to provide a framework for considering the risks and impacts arising from climate change on the insurance sector in the UK.

TITLE: Luxembourg's Climate Finance Task Force
DESCRIPTION: Luxembourg's Climate Finance Task Force (CFTF) was established in 2015 to bring together the Luxembourg Government and industry experts in order to develop initiatives in the field of green and sustainable finance and to consolidate the position of Luxembourg as an international center for green finance.

TITLE: Spain Updates Good Governance Code of Listed Companies with Corporate Social Responsibility Recommendations
DESCRIPTION: Spain's Unified Good Governance Code of Listed Companies, approved in 2006, was updated in 2013 to adapt or eliminate recommendations affected by new legislation and in 2015 to incorporate recommendations that deal specifically with corporate social responsibility (CSR).

TITLE: New Jersey Energy Resilience Bank
INSTITUTIONS: Institution(s): New Jersey Economic Development Authority
DESCRIPTION: The New Jersey Energy Resilience Bank was established as part of the state’s effort to minimize the potential impacts of future major power outages and increase energy resiliency.

TITLE: Vanuatu Infrastructure Strategic Investment Plan
INSTITUTIONS: Institution(s): Government of the Republic of Vanuatu
DESCRIPTION: Vanuatu Infrastructure Strategic Investment Plan aims at implementing strategic infrastructure investments across seven economic and social sectors to support sustainable socio-economic development.

TITLE: A Bulletin Issued by the United States Department of Labor Clarifies that Environmental, Social, and Governance (ESG) Factors Can Be Part of Investment Decision Making
DESCRIPTION: In 2015, the United States Department of Labor's Employee Benefits Security Administration issued an Interpretive Bulletin that clarified that environmental, social, and governance (ESG) factors can be part of primary analysis of prudent investment decision making.

TITLE: Sustainability Amendments to Malaysia's Main Market Listing Requirements
DESCRIPTION: Under the 2015 Amendments to Malaysia's Main Market Listing Requirements relating to Sustainability, listed issuers are required to disclose a statement on the management of material economic, environmental, and social (“EES”) risks and opportunities (“Sustainability Statement”) in their annual reports.

TITLE: Warehouse for Energy Efficiency Loans (WHEEL)
INSTITUTIONS: Institution(s): National Association of State Energy Officials (NASEO)
DESCRIPTION: The Warehouse for Energy Efficiency Loans (WHEEL) is a public-private partnership to create a national financing platform to bring low-cost, large-scale capital to government and utility sponsored residential energy efficiency loan programmes.

TITLE: Disaster Risk Finance and Insurance Strategy
INSTITUTIONS: Institution(s): Philippine Insurance Commission, Local Governments, World Bank, Insurance Stakeholders
DESCRIPTION: The Philippines’ Disaster Risk Finance and Insurance Strategy is a parametric insurance pooling facility for local government units, to be insured through the Government Service Insurance System (GSIS).

TITLE: Vnesheconombank (VEB) Sustainability Roadmap
DESCRIPTION: In 2015 VEB published its Sustainability roadmap for 2015-2020 which includes commitments on sustainable finance

TITLE: Revisions to Financial Condition Examiners Handbook
INSTITUTIONS: Institution(s): National Association of Insurance Commissioners (NAIC)
DESCRIPTION: The National Association of Insurance Commissioners (NAIC) requires that insurance companies disclose to regulators and investors the financial risks that they face from climate change, as well as actions that the companies are taking to respond to those risks.

TITLE: Design of a Sustainable Financial System: Swiss Team Input into Inquiry into the Design of a Sustainable Financial System (UN Environment Inquiry)
INSTITUTIONS: Institution(s): Federal Ministry of the Environment, Swiss Confederation
DESCRIPTION: The Swiss team for the Inquiry into the Design of a Sustainable Financial System (UN Environment Inquiry) gathers representatives of the financial sector, NGOs, and academia as well as government representatives to reflect on the Inquiry’s questions regarding a financial system aligned to sustainable development.

TITLE: California has Issued a USD 300 Million Green Bond
INSTITUTIONS: Institution(s): The California State Treasurer's Office
DESCRIPTION: In October 2014, California issued a USD 300 million green bond.

TITLE: The Brazilian Securities Commission (CVM) Instruction No. 480/2009 Requires Listed Companies to Include Environmental Information in their Annual Reports
DESCRIPTION: The Brazilian Securities Commission (CVM) Instruction No. 480/2009, which provides for the registration of issuers (foreign and domestic) of securities admitted to trading on regulated markets in Brazil, requires listed companies to include environmental information in their annual reports.

TITLE: Dutch Pensions Act Requires Funds to Report on Environmental and Social Issues (Article 135)
DESCRIPTION: Since 2014, the Pensions Act (Section 135-4), has required pension funds to state in their annual reports how their investment policies take into account the environment and climate, human rights, and social relations.

TITLE: California Senate Bill 185 Prohibits State Pension Funds From Making New or Renewing Existing Investments in Thermal Coal Companies
DESCRIPTION: California Senate Bill 185 on Public Retirement Systems prohibits state pension funds (CalPERS and CalSTRS) from making new investments or renewing existing investments of public employee retirement funds in thermal coal companies.

TITLE: The Environmental Impact Index
INSTITUTIONS: Institution(s): Israel Ministry of Environmental Protection
DESCRIPTION: The Environmental Impact Index analyses Israel's largest publicly traded companies based on their impact on the environment and compliance with requirements and standards.

TITLE: Directive on Promoting Green Credit Growth and Environmental and Social Risks Management in Credit Granting Activities
DESCRIPTION: Vietnam’s Directive on Promoting Green Credit Growth and Environmental and Social Risks Management in Credit Granting Activities (the Directive) seeks to promote a green economy and encourages all credit institutions to incorporate environmental and social (E&S) risks into their transactions.

TITLE: Norges Bank's Principles for Responsible Investment Management
DESCRIPTION: In 2015, Norges Bank published Principles for Responsible Investment Management, which covers four key areas—standard setting, ownership, risk management, and observation and exclusion.

TITLE: Resolution 4.327/2014: Financial Institutions Socio-Environmental Responsibility
DESCRIPTION: Resolution 4.327/2014 lists guidelines to be observed upon establishing and deploying Socio-environmental Responsibility policies by financial Institutions.

TITLE: Germany's Act on the Supervision of Insurance Undertakings Requires Pension Funds to Report on Ethical, Social, and Ecological Considerations
INSTITUTIONS: Institution(s): Sustainable Insurance Forum and Bundesanstalt für Finanzdienstleistungsaufsicht (BaFin)
DESCRIPTION: Germany’s Act on the Supervision of Insurance Undertakings (Versicherungsaufsichtsgesetz, or VAG) requires pension funds to inform its beneficiaries in writing of whether, and, if so, how, it takes ethical, social and ecological interests into account in the way it invests the contributions paid

TITLE: Mongolian Sustainable Finance Principles and Sector Guidelines
INSTITUTIONS: Institution(s): Mongonlian Banker's Association and Mongolian Central Bank
DESCRIPTION: Mongolia's Sustainable Finance Principles and related Sector Guidelines were adopted in 2014 to provide a voluntary framework to help local banks integrate environmental and social considerations into their lending decisions and product design.

TITLE: Guidelines for Information Disclosure on Securities Market (Circular 155/2015/TT-BTC)
INSTITUTIONS: Institution(s): State Securities Commission (SSC) of Vietnam
DESCRIPTION: Vietnam's Guidelines for Information Disclosure on Securities Market (Circular 155/2015/TT-BTC) requires listed companies to report on their impacts on the environment and society.

TITLE: Notice on Green Credit Key Performance Indicators (No. 186)
DESCRIPTION: This Notice stipulates that all banking institutions are required to facilitate and thoroughly carry out self-assessment of their green credit implementation following the requirements of the Green Credit Key Performance Indicators.

TITLE: Regulation on Socio-environmental Risk Management of Financial Firms in Peru (SBS N°01-2015)
INSTITUTIONS: Institution(s): Superintendency of Banking, Insurance and Private Pension Fund Administrators (SBS)
DESCRIPTION: This paper describes the key design features of Peru's regulation on socio-environmental risk management of financial firms (SBS N°01-2015), which aims to promote sound practices for financial institutions exposed to such risks.

TITLE: France's Energy and Ecological Transition for Climate Label
INSTITUTIONS: Institution(s): Ministry for an Ecological and Solidarity Transition
DESCRIPTION: France's Energy and Ecological Transition for the Climate (Transition énergétique et écologique pour le climat, or TEEC) label is the first public label for private investments in the green economy.

TITLE: Panama's Strategic Framework for the Financial Management of Disaster Risk
DESCRIPTION: Panama adopted a Strategic Framework for the Financial Management of Disaster Risk in 2014 (Executive Decree 578), which includes the following five pillars: (i) identification, quantification, and understanding of fiscal risk due to disasters; (ii) incorporation of disaster risk analysis in the planning of public investment; (iii) formulation of components for developing and implementing risk retention and transfer instruments; (iv) development of the domestic insurance market; and (v) strengthening of DICRE (the Directorate of Investments, Concessions, and Risks of the State—the government unit responsible for managing fiscal risk of disasters) so it can fulfill its role in de-signing and implementing financial protection strategies.

TITLE: The Budget Bill for 2016
DESCRIPTION: The Budget Bill is the Government's proposal for central government budget revenue and expenditure for the fiscal year. In the Budget Bill for 2016, financial sector are mandated to contribute to sustainable development as part of "generational goal," in order to enhance national green competitiveness.

TITLE: Environmental and Social Risk Management of Financial Institutions in Peru (Resolution 1928/2015)
INSTITUTIONS: Institution(s): Superintendency of Banking, Insurance and Private Pension Fund Administrators (SBS)
DESCRIPTION: Resolution 1928/2015 requires financial institutions to manage environmental and social (E&S) risks for projects over USD 10 million, including evaluating E&S risks to projects and project primary suppliers as well as reporting to regulators and clients.

TITLE: Corporate Social Responsibility (CSR) Implementation Guide for Canadian Business
INSTITUTIONS: Institution(s): Government of Canada, Innovation, Science and Economic Development Canda
DESCRIPTION: The Corporate Social Responsibility (CSR) Implementation Guide for Canadian Business provides practical advice for how companies should approach CSR, including making its business case, developing a strategy, and monitoring outcomes.

TITLE: A 2015 Report has Proposed a Roadmap to Finance a Low-Carbon Economy in France
DESCRIPTION: A 2015 report by the Canfin-Grandjean Commission has proposed paths of action to mobilize increased public and private funding in the fight against climate change.

TITLE: Sustainable and Responsible Investment Sukuk Framework
DESCRIPTION: Malaysia's Sustainable and Responsible Investment (SRI) Sukuk Framework provides a regulatory framework to facilitate more green, social, and sustainable financing.

TITLE: Amendment to the Accounting Act 237
DESCRIPTION: The new Bulgarian Accountancy Act implements EU Directive 2014/95/EU and prescribes that large enterprises which are public interest enterprises and which, at 31 December of the reporting period, exceed the criterion of the average number of employees during the financial year of 500 people, shall include a non-financial declaration in their management report.

TITLE: Article 173-VI (for investors) and Article 173-IV (for companies) of France's Law on Energy Transition for Green Growth
DESCRIPTION: France's 2015 Energy Transition Law requires institutional investors and companies to provide information on the way that they take into account climate change as well as environmental and social factors into their strategies and decision making (Article 173-VI for investors, and Article 173-IV for companies).

TITLE: Flood Re Makes the Flood Cover Part of Household Insurance Policies More Affordable
INSTITUTIONS: Institution(s): HM Government and Insurers - Prudential Regulation Authority (PRA) and Financial Conduct Authority (FCA)
COUNTRY: Country: United Kingdom of Great Britain and Northern Ireland
DESCRIPTION: Flood Re is a reinsurance scheme in the United Kingdom that aims to make the flood cover part of household insurance policies more affordable.

TITLE: Peru Adopts Resolution that Includes Mandatory Sustainability Reporting (Resolución SMV Nº 033-2015-SMV/01)
INSTITUTIONS: Institution(s): Superintendencia del Mercado de Valores (SMV)
DESCRIPTION: Peru’s Capital Markets Superintendency (SMV) has adopted a Resolution (SMV Nº 033-2015-SMV/01) that includes mandatory sustainability reporting, with a “comply or explain” approach.

TITLE: The Corporate Social Responsibility (CSR) Strategy, 2019-2025, of De Nederlandsche Bank (DNB)
DESCRIPTION:
The Netherland’s central bank—De Nederlandsche Bank (DNB)—has published a Corporate Social Responsibility (CSR) Strategy for 2019-2025, which centres on two themes:
Sustainable economic growth that has no harmful effects o

TITLE: National Pension Fund Investments to Include ESG Considerations (National Pension Service Act, Chapter VI Article 102 (4))
DESCRIPTION: When managing and operating Korea's National Pension Fund, environmental, social, and governance (ESG) factors applicable to the investment targets may be considered, as stipulated in Korea's National Pension Service Act (Chapter VI Article 102 (4)).

TITLE: Sustainable Finance Guiding Principles Adopted by Kenya's Banking Industry
INSTITUTIONS: Institution(s): Kenyan Banking Association and Central Bank of Kenya
DESCRIPTION: Kenya's banking industry, through their umbrella body the Kenya Bankers Association (KBA), has adopted Sustainable Finance Guiding Principles to help balance business goals with the economy's development priorities and socio-environmental concerns.

TITLE: New York's Green Bank to Increase Investments in Clean Energy Markets
DESCRIPTION: New York's Green Bank is a state-sponsored, specialized financial entity working with the private sector to increase investments into New York’s clean energy markets, thereby creating a more efficient, reliable, and sustainable energy system.

TITLE: Natural Capital Financing Facility
INSTITUTIONS: Institution(s): European Commission and European Investment Bank
DESCRIPTION: The European Investment Bank (EIB) and the European Commission (EC) have partnered to create the Natural Capital Financing Facility (NCFF)—a financial instrument that supports projects delivering on biodiversity and climate adaptation through tailored loans and investments, backed by a European Union (EU) guarantee.

TITLE: Russia's Code of Corporate Governance (Article 69) Recommends Joint Stock Companies to Assess Financial and Non-Financial Risks
DESCRIPTION: Under article 69 of the Russian Code of Corporate Governance, the board of directors of joint stock companies are advised to assess financial and non-financial risks, including environmental, social, ethical, and operational risks, as well as establish tolerable levels of risk in these areas.

TITLE: The Argentine Securities Commission (regulated under Law N° 26.831) is Among the Few Market Regulators with Sustainability in its Mandate
INSTITUTIONS: Institution(s): Comisión Nacional de Valores (the Argentine Securities and Exchange Commission)
DESCRIPTION: The Argentine Securities Commission (Comisión Nacional de Valores, “CNV”)—the agency responsible for the promotion, supervision, and control of the country’s Capital Market, which is regulated under Law N° 26.831—is one of the few market regulators internationally with sustainability in its mandate.

TITLE: Resource Efficiency and Fiduciary Duties of Investors
DESCRIPTION: This report investigates the application of fiduciary duty in the European Union (EU) and the state of play on the inclusion of environmental and resource efficiency factors into the fiduciary duties of institutional investors.

TITLE: Singapore's Code of Corporate Governance 2012 Revision Includes Sustainability Issues
DESCRIPTION: Singapore's Code of Corporate Governance, which was first issued in 2001 by the Corporate Governance Committee (“CGC”), was subsequently revised in 2005 and again in 2012; the latest version now states that "the Board's role is to consider sustainability issues e.g. environmental and social factors, as part of its strategic formulation."

TITLE: Japan Green Fund (Japan Green Finance Organisation)
DESCRIPTION: In July 2013, Japan’s Green Fund commenced operations, following the Minister of Environment's January 2013 announcement of the Finance Initiative to build a Low-Carbon Society, which highlighted the need to use private capital to tackle global warming.

TITLE: Amendment to the Companies Act of 2006 Includes New Environmental, Social, and Governance (ESG) Disclosure Requirements
COUNTRY: Country: United Kingdom of Great Britain and Northern Ireland
DESCRIPTION: In 2013, the United Kingdom adopted an amendment to the Companies Act of 2006 that includes several provisions related to environmental, social, and governance (ESG) reporting and disclosure.

TITLE: Danish Corporate Reporting on Human Rights and Climate (Financial Statements Act, Amendment 2012)
DESCRIPTION: The Danish Parliament has adopted an amendment to its Financial Statements Act that requires businesses to specifically report on their human rights and climate issues and impacts, regardless of whether or not they are included in their CSR policies.

TITLE: Additional Directive (2014: 158) Aims to Improve How Fund Managers Integrate Sustainability
DESCRIPTION: The Swedish Government’s review of mutual fund managers, as stipulated under Directive 2014:139, has been expanded under Directive 2014:158 to propose measures to improve information and comparability on how fund managers integrate sustainability aspects such as environmental and climate issues, human rights, working conditions, and combating corruption.

TITLE: CODIM Pronouncement no. 13 and 14, 2012
INSTITUTIONS: Institution(s): Brazilian Steering Committee for Information Disclosure to the Market (CODIM)
DESCRIPTION: Pronouncement 13 sets up annual report guidelines, in order to foster best practices in reporting, information disclosure, and corporate governance.

TITLE: Hawaii's Green Infrastructure Authority Makes Clean Energy Investments More Accessible and Affordable
DESCRIPTION: Hawaii's Green Infrastructure Authority (HGIA), which was established in 2013, makes clean energy investments more accessible and affordable for low- and moderate-income (LMI) single family residential homeowners and renters, multi-family rental projects, small businesses, and non-profit organizations.

TITLE: Pakistan's Corporate Social Responsibility Voluntary Guidelines
INSTITUTIONS: Institution(s): Securities and Exchange Commission of Pakistan
DESCRIPTION: Under Pakistan's Corporate Social Responsibility (CSR) Voluntary Guidelines, the boards of directors of registered entities are encouraged to take ownership of the formulation, adoption, and implementation of their company's CSR policy.

TITLE: Forest Code (law 12.651-2012)
DESCRIPTION: Brazil’s Forest Code (Law 12.651 – 2012) establishes a regulatory framework for land use and environmental conservation on rural properties, with the purpose of protecting native vegetation.

TITLE: Green Posting System - Corporate Disclosure
DESCRIPTION: Korea's Financial Services Commission's Green Posting System requires firms to post their greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions and energy usage, as well green technology certification.

TITLE: Transboundary Haze Pollution Act
DESCRIPTION: Singapore's Transboundary Haze Pollution Act criminalizes activities that contribute to haze pollution and introduces corporate liability for international firms, including financial institutions, that start fires or allow concessions to burn.

TITLE: National Impact Initiative
DESCRIPTION: On June 2013, the United States launched the National Impact Initiative (NII) to expand the use of impact investing as an element of the government's strategies for economic growth and global development.

TITLE: The European Investment Bank's (EIB's) Energy Lending Criteria Include an Emission Performance Standard
DESCRIPTION: The European Investment Bank's (EIB's) Energy Lending Criteria introduced an emission performance standard (EPS) to ensure that all fossil fuel power generation projects financed by the EIB are in line with member states' commitments to EU climate policy.

TITLE: China's Green Credit Guidelines
DESCRIPTION: In 2012, the China Banking Regulatory Commission (CBRC) issued Green Credit Guidelines that aim to encourage banking institutions to develop green credit and adopt stronger environmental and social risk management.

TITLE: Sustainability Development Roadmap for Listed Companies
INSTITUTIONS: Institution(s): Securities and Exchange Commission of Thailand (SEC)
DESCRIPTION: Thailand's Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) has conducted assessments on circumstances that could pose potential impacts on the sustainable development of listed companies.

TITLE: Australia's Green Bank—the Clean Energy Finance Corporation, Facilitates Increased Investments in Emissions Reduction
DESCRIPTION: Australia's Green Bank—the Clean Energy Finance Corporation (CEFC)—was established to facilitate increased flows of finance to help Australia cut its greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions. CEFC is investing AU$10 billion to address some of Australia’s toughest emissions challenges—in agriculture, cleantech innovation, energy generation and storage, infrastructure, property, transport, and waste.

TITLE: Vermont Clean Energy Loan Fund
DESCRIPTION: Vermont's Clean Energy Loan Fund was established in 2013 to consolidate clean energy programs that existed under the Vermont Economic Development Authority (VEDA), supporting renewable energy, agricultural energy, energy efficiency, and small business conservation.

TITLE: The EU Energy Efficiency Financial Institutions Group
INSTITUTIONS: Institution(s): European Commission Directorate-General for Energy (DG Energy) and United Nations Environment Program Finance Initiative (UNEP FI)
DESCRIPTION: The European Union's (EU's) Energy Efficiency Financial Institutions Group (EEFIG), which was established in 2013, has created an open dialogue and work platform for public and private financial institutions, industry representatives, and sector experts to identify the barriers to the long-term financing for energy efficiency and propose policy and market solutions to them.

TITLE: Notification on Monitoring and Reporting of Turkey's Greenhouse Gas Emissions
INSTITUTIONS: Institution(s): Ministry of Environment and Urbanism
DESCRIPTION: This Notification sets forth the principles and procedures for the monitoring and reporting of Turkey's greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions.

TITLE: The Kay Review of UK Equity Markets and Long-Term Decision-Making Finds that Short-termism is an Underlying Problem
COUNTRY: Country: United Kingdom of Great Britain and Northern Ireland
DESCRIPTION: The Kay Review recommends that there should be a shift in the culture of the stock market. The report finds that short-termism is an underlying problem in UK equity markets, principally caused by a misalignment of incentives within the investment chain and the displacement of trust relationships by a culture based on transactions and trading.

TITLE: India's Listing Obligations and Disclosure Requirements
INSTITUTIONS: Institution(s): Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI)
DESCRIPTION: India's Listing Obligations and Disclosure Requirements Regulations, which were adopted in 2012 and amended in 2016 and 2018, require the top 500 listed companies based on market capitalization to produce Business Responsibility Reports, which are to be included in their annual reports.

TITLE: White Paper on Financing Ecological Transition
INSTITUTIONS: Institution(s): Directorate General of the Treasury and thew Office of the Commissioner General for Sustainable Development
DESCRIPTION: The White Paper on Financing Ecological Transition is based on four principles.

TITLE: Corporate Social Responsibility (CSR) Law No. 8488
DESCRIPTION: Argentina's Corporate Social Responsibility (CSR) Law, No. 8488, requires an annual CSR Report (Balance de Responsabilidad Social y Ambiental) for all companies with more than 300 employees and a superior gross profit established by the Sepyme (Secretaría de la Pequeña y Mediana Empresa) for SMEs.

TITLE: FIji's Agriculture and Renewable Energy Loans Ratio
DESCRIPTION: Under Fiji's Agriculture and Renewable Energy Loans Ratio, commercial banks must allocate 4 percent of their deposits, and similar liabilities in loans, to the agriculture (including forestry and fisheries) sector, and 2 percent to the renewable energy sector.

TITLE: Requirements to Join the Green Bond Segment of the Johannesburg Stock Exchange
DESCRIPTION: Green bonds from the Johannesburg Stock Exchange (JSE) are reviewed against clear criteria in order to provide the green bond market with trust and assurance around the environmental credentials of the bonds.

TITLE: The Brazilian Circular on Internal Process of Capital Adequacy Assessment (No. 3,547/2011) Requires Banks to Include Social and Environmental Risks When Assessing Their Capital Needs
DESCRIPTION: The Brazilian Circular on Internal Process of Capital Adequacy Assessment (No. 3,547/2011) includes a requirement for banks to demonstrate how they evaluate the risk arising from exposure to social and environmental damage caused by their activities when assessing how much capital is needed to cover a range of operational and financial risks.

TITLE: Australia's Superannuation Governance Policy (Standard No. 20) Requires Environmental, Social, and Governance (ESG) Risk Management and Disclosure
DESCRIPTION: The Australian Financial Services Council (FSC) issued the Superannuation Governance Policy (Standard No. 20) in 2013 to promote strong governance arrangements by trustees of superannuation entities.

TITLE: India's Companies Act of 2013 Includes Provisions on Corporate Social Responsibility
DESCRIPTION: India's Companies Act of 2013 stipulates that companies of a certain size shall constitute a Corporate Social Responsibility Committee, which shall formulate and recommend to the Board a Corporate Social Responsibility Policy (Clause 135).

TITLE: Corporate Responsibility Regulation in Indonesia (Regulation No. 47/2012)
DESCRIPTION: Indonesia's corporate social responsibility regulation (No. 47/2012) stipulates that all companies that manage or utilise natural resources or that impact natural resources are required to fulfill social and environmental responsibilities.

TITLE: European Commission's Investment Plan for Europe, or 'Juncker Plan'
DESCRIPTION: The Investment Plan for Europe, the so-called Juncker Plan, has three objectives: to remove obstacles to investment; to provide visibility and technical assistance to investment projects; and to make smarter use of financial resources.

TITLE: Brazil's Resolution (4,008/2011) on Financing Climate Mitigation and Adaptation Projects
DESCRIPTION: Brazil's Resolution 4,008/2011 sets out rules on financing climate mitigation and adaptation projects. It established credit lines for climate-friendly lending, backed by resources from the National Plan for Climate Change (FNMC).

TITLE: Prudential Practice Guide on Investment Governance (SPG 530)
DESCRIPTION: The Prudential Practice Guide on Investment Governance states that a superannuation trustee may adopt an investment strategy that has an environmental, social, and governance (ESG) focus, so long as it can demonstrate appropriate analysis to support its formulation, including being mindful of exposing the interests of beneficiaries to undue risk.

TITLE: Indonesia's Green Lending Model Guidelines for Mini Hydro Power Plant Projects
DESCRIPTION: In collaboration with Indonesia's Ministry of Environment and Forestry and USAID, the Bank Indonesia developed voluntary Green Lending Model Guidelines for Mini Hydro Power Plant Projects for banks in 2013.

TITLE: Italy's Provisions on the Process of Implementing the Investment Policy Require Communication of Ethical, Environment, and/or Social Criteria
DESCRIPTION: Italy's Commission for the Supervision of Pension Funds (La Commissione di vigilanza sui fondi pensione, or COVIP) adopted a Resolution on 16 March 2012 that requires the communication of any ethical, environmental, and/or social criteria in the statement of investment principles (see Articles 4-5 of 'Provisions on the Process of Implementing the Investment Policy').

TITLE: Law Commission Report
COUNTRY: Country: United Kingdom of Great Britain and Northern Ireland
DESCRIPTION: The independent commission report looked at the investment market through the lens of pensions. The report concludes that trustees should take into account factors which are financially material to the performance of an investment. Where trustees think ethical or environmental, social or governance (ESG) issues are financially material they should take them into account.

TITLE: St. Vincent and the Grenadines National Economic and Social Development Plan 2013 - 2025
INSTITUTIONS: Institution(s): Government of Saint Vincent and the Grenadines
COUNTRY: Country: Saint Vincent and the Grenadines
DESCRIPTION: In January 2013, the Government of St. Vincent and the Grenadines introduced the National Economic and Social Development Plan 2013 - 2025.

TITLE: The UK's Green Investment Group is Making Green Infrastructure Investments and Developing Projects to Accelerate the Transition to a Green Economy
COUNTRY: Country: United Kingdom of Great Britain and Northern Ireland
DESCRIPTION: The United Kingdom's Green Investment Group (previously the UK Green Investment Bank) is a specialist green investor with a mission to accelerate the transition to a greener global economy by making new green infrastructure investments and developing new projects.

TITLE: Lebanon Incentivised Investments in Eco-Friendly Projects (Circular No. 313)
DESCRIPTION: In 2013, the Bank of Lebanon (Banque du Liban, or BDL) issued Circular No. 313 to provide incentives for investments that focus on eco-friendly projects, including energy efficiency, renewable energy, and certified green buildings.

TITLE: The Malaysian Code on Corporate Governance Includes a Recommendation on Promoting Sustainability
DESCRIPTION: The Malaysian Code on Corporate Governance focuses on clarifying the role of the board in providing leadership, enhancing board effectiveness through strengthening its composition, and reinforcing its independence. Recommendation 1.4 states that "The board should ensure that the company's strategies promote sustainability."

TITLE: Nigerian Sustainable Banking Principles and Guidance Note
INSTITUTIONS: Institution(s): Central bank of Nigeria/Nigerian Banking Association
DESCRIPTION: In 2012, the Nigerian Bankers' Committee approved the adoption of the Sustainable Banking Principles by banks, discount houses, and development finance institutions.

TITLE: Malaysian Code for Institutional Investors
DESCRIPTION: Malaysia's Code for Institutional Investors is intended to give institutional investors guidance on effective exercise of stewardship responsibilities to ensure delivery of sustainable long-term value to their ultimate beneficiaries or clients.

TITLE: Colombia's Protocol Verde (Green Protocol)
INSTITUTIONS: Institution(s): Ministry of Environment and Sustainable Development
DESCRIPTION: In 2012, the Green Protocol was signed by the Colombian Government and some of the most relevant commercial and development banks associated in ASOBANCARIA—the representative association of the Colombian financial sector. The Green Protocol is a voluntary framework with guidelines that aims to promote green finance.

TITLE: Connecticut's Green Bank is Helping to Make Green Energy More Accessible and Affordable
DESCRIPTION: The Connecticut Green Bank (CGB) is a quasi-public corporation that works with private-sector investors to create low-cost, long-term sustainable financing for green energy in order to increase its affordability and accessibility for homeowners, businesses, and institutions.

TITLE: Lebanon Extends Its Subsidized Loan Scheme in Green Sectors with an Additional USD 331 Million
DESCRIPTION: In 2013, the Bank of Lebanon (Banque du Liban, or BDL) issued Circular No. 346 to extend its subsidized loan scheme in green sectors implemented under Circular No. 236 by adding a package of USD 331 million.

TITLE: Principles for Financial Action Towards a Sustainable Society
DESCRIPTION: The Principles for Financial Action Towards a Sustainable Society were established in Japan to set a policy across the financial industry in order to allow cooperative actions to be taken on various environmental, social, and governance (ESG) issues, and directly promote such efforts through their core business operations.

TITLE: National Climate Change Investment Plan
DESCRIPTION: In 2014, Malawi government published its National Climate Change Investment Plan which identifies the four key priority areas to promote climate change management in Malawi: adaptation; mitigation; climate change research, technology development and transfer; and capacity building.

TITLE: Law 1523/2012 Expands the Role of Colombia's National Fund for Disaster Risk Management (FNGRD)
DESCRIPTION: With Law 1523/2012, Colombia initiated an ambitious reform process to establish an effective disaster risk governance framework that anchors resilience in the national policy agenda.

TITLE: Norway Adopts Amendment to the Accounting Act of 1998 that Requires Corporate Social Responsibility (CSR) Reporting by Large Companies
DESCRIPTION: The Norwegian Parliament passed the proposed ‘Act amending the Accounting Act and certain other Acts (Social Responsibility Reporting)’ on 9 April 2013.

TITLE: German Sustainability Code
INSTITUTIONS: Institution(s): German Council for Sustainable Development
DESCRIPTION: The German Sustainability Code includes 20 criteria and a checklist on what companies should report on with regards to sustainability.

TITLE: China's Green Credit Statistics System
DESCRIPTION: The China Banking Regulatory Commission (CBRC) launched a Notice on the two documents that form the Green Credit Statistics System (GCSS) for banking institutions when categorizing green credit portfolio (YINJIANBANFA, 2013, No. 185; and YINJIANTONGTONG, 2014, No. 60)

TITLE: Lebanon Issued Circular No. 236 to Facilitate Financing in Green Sectors
DESCRIPTION: In 2010, the Bank of Lebanon (Banque du Liban, or BDL) issued Circular No. 236 to facilitate financing and investments in green sectors by exempting commerical banks from part of the required reserves, enabling the finance of these projects at lower costs.

TITLE: National Strategy for Climate Change and Low Carbon Development
DESCRIPTION: In October 2011, the Republic of Rwanda released its Green Growth and Climate Resilience National Strategy for Climate Change and Low Carbon Development.

TITLE: India's National Voluntary Guidelines on Social, Environmental, and Economic Responsibilities of Business
INSTITUTIONS: Institution(s): Government of India, Ministry of Corporate Affairs
DESCRIPTION: The guidelines, which are designed to be used by all businesses in India, contain a list of KPIs on which companies should report

TITLE: Pakistani Regulation (General Order: SRO 983(I)) Requires Public Companies to Disclose Corporate Social Responsibility (CSR) Activities
INSTITUTIONS: Institution(s): Securities and Exchange Commission of Pakistan
DESCRIPTION: In 2009, Pakistan passed a regulation (General Order: SRO 983 (I)) that requires all public companies to provide mandatory descriptive as well as monetary disclosures of their corporate social responsibility (CSR) activities undertaken during each financial year.

TITLE: Guidance Opinions on Strengthening the Oversight of Public Companies ("Green Securities Policy")
INSTITUTIONS: Institution(s): Ministry of Ecology and Environment
DESCRIPTION: In 2008, China launched the Green Securities Policy to increase sustainability practices among companies listed on Chinese stock markets. One of the integral components of the policy is the environmental disclosure regulation, which directs publicly traded Chinese companies in 14 highly polluting industrieds to report required environmental disclosure.

TITLE: Malaysian Green Technology Corporation
INSTITUTIONS: Institution(s): Ministry of Energy, Green Technology and Water
DESCRIPTION: The Malaysian Green Technology Corporation (i.e. GreenTech Malaysia) is a government agency with the mandate to spearhead the development and promotion of green technology as a strategic engine for socio-economic growth and sustainability.

TITLE: Ethiopia’s Climate Resilient Green Economy Strategy 2011
INSTITUTIONS: Institution(s): Federal Democratic Republic of Ethiopia
DESCRIPTION: In November 2011, the Republic of Ethiopia launched its vision to build a Climate Resilient Green Economy (CRGE) by 2025.

TITLE: Malaysia's Corporate Governance Blueprint
DESCRIPTION: Malaysia's Corporate Governance Blueprint sets out the strategic directions and specific action plans to be implemented over a five-year period in order to raise the standards of corporate governance in the Malaysian capital market.

TITLE: Bangladesh's Refinancing Scheme for Renewable Energy and Green Financing
DESCRIPTION: To promote renewable energy and environmentally friendly financial activity, Bangladesh Bank has formulated a Refinancing Scheme for Renewable Energy and Green Financing.

TITLE: Socially responsible and sustainable development savings account (Livret de Developpement durable)
DESCRIPTION: The CODEVI as of 1 January 2007 has been renamed the LDD (Livret de Développement Durable), and banks must use a portion of these funds to offer preferential loans for domestic energy conservation projects.

TITLE: Central Bank of Tanzania’s objective of supporting sustainable economic growth
DESCRIPTION: The mandate of the Central Bank of Tanzania includes an explicit objective for the promotion of sustainable economic development.

TITLE: National Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Law (Republic Act 10121)
DESCRIPTION: The Philippines' National Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Law (Republic Act 10121) provides a macro-level framework for addressing disaster risk.

TITLE: Russia’s Regulation on Information Disclosure (Order 11-46/pz-n, 2011)
DESCRIPTION: Russia’s Regulation on Information Disclosure (Order 11-46/pz-n, 2011) states that annual reports should contain significant volume of non-financial information on results in key areas of activity, including the use of energy resources, risk factors, corporate governance and remuneration, and voluntary adherence with the Russian Code of Corporate Governance.

TITLE: Law on Limited Liability Companies (40/2007) Requires Reporting on Environmental and Social Responsibility
DESCRIPTION: Indonesia's Law on Limited Liability Company (40/2007) requires companies to submit annual reports with social and environmental responsibility information and states that companies having business activities in the field of and/or related to natural resources are obliged to perform their Social and Environmental Responsibility.

TITLE: China's Management Directory of Listed Companies Environmental Protection Industry Classification
DESCRIPTION: For the industries listed on the Management Directory of Listed Companies Environmental Protection Industry Classification, China requires that an environmental assessment is conducted before initiating an initial public offering (IPO) or obtaining refinancing from banks.

TITLE: Sustainability Fund Act of Brunei
INSTITUTIONS: Institution(s): Ministry of Finance and Economy, Brunei Darussalam
DESCRIPTION: In March 2011, the Government of Brunei enacted the Sustainability Fund Act.

TITLE: Financial Reporting Accounting Standard No. 26
DESCRIPTION: Portugal's Financial Reporting Accounting Standard No. 26 adopts the European Commission's recommendation from 2001 on the recognition, measurement, and disclosure of environmental issues in the annual accounts and annual reports of companies.

TITLE: Spain's Sustainable Economy Law Requires Disclosure of Annual Sustainability Reports
DESCRIPTION: Spain's Sustainable Economy Law requires government-sponsored commercial companies or state-owned companies to file annual sustainability reports.

TITLE: Resolution 3545/2008: Rural Credit – Environmental Compliance in the Amazon
DESCRIPTION: Resolution 3545/2008 requires financial institutions and rural producers to have documentation proof of compliance with environmental regulations (particularly land use regulations set out in the Forest Code) to have access to subsidised rural credit in the Amazon biome region.

TITLE: Principles of Corporate Governance of State-Owned Enterprises (Resolution of the Cabinet Council 49/2007)
DESCRIPTION: Portugal’s Principles of Corporate Governance (Resolution 49/2007) defines best practices to be undertaken by public companies, which is substantially based on the OECD Guidelines on Corporate Governance of State-Owned Enterprises (2005).

TITLE: Brazilian Resolution 3.896/2010: Rural Credit for Low-Carbon Agriculture
DESCRIPTION: Resolution 3.896/2010 is a credit line which allows farmers to adhere to the guidelines of the Program for Reducing Greenhouse Gas Emissions (ABC Program) in the Brazilian Development Bank (BNDES) Framework.

TITLE: Mexican Pension Funds Regulator (CONSAR) Issues Rule With Obligation to Analyse Companies’ Social Responsibility
DESCRIPTION: CONSAR, the Mexican pension funds regulator, published rules regarding investment strategies that included, for the first time, a general reference to an obligation to analyse companies’ social responsibility credentials.

TITLE: Framework Act on Low Carbon
DESCRIPTION: The Korean National Assembly enacted the Framework Act on Low Carbon, Green Growth in January 2010 to provide the legal basis for implementing policy measures that address climate change and energy issues and promote eco-efficient development.

TITLE: Brazil's Green Protocol
DESCRIPTION: Brazil's Green Protocol is a voluntary banking commitment that aims to encourage sustainable development and socio-environmental responsibility through various principles, including considering socio-environmental impacts and costs in asset management and in client and project risk analyses as well as incorporating socio-environmental criteria in credit analyses.

TITLE: Coverage Limits Increase for Switzerland’s Mandatory Insurance Against Damage by Natural Disasters for Chattels and Buildings
DESCRIPTION: In Switzerland, it has been mandatory since 1993 to purchase insurance to cover damage to chattels and buildings by natural forces (high water, floods, storms, hail, avalanches, snow pressure, rockslides, rockfalls, and landslides); and in January 2007, an increase in coverage limits (to CHF 1 billion) entered into force.

TITLE: Guidance on Environmental Reporting (CSA Staff Notice 51-333)
DESCRIPTION: Canada published Guidance on Environmental Reporting (CSA Staff Notice 51-333) in 2010 to guide issuers on existing disclosure requirements relating to environmental matters under securities legislation.

TITLE: Amendment to South Africa's Pension Funds Act of 1956 (Amendment of Regulation 28)
DESCRIPTION: South Africa's amendment to its Pension Funds Act (of Regulation 28 under Section 36) provides a set of principles on investment practices and rules stipulating asset allocation limits as well as the consideration of environmental, social, and governance (ESG) factors.

TITLE: Certificate of Corporate Social and Environmental Responsibility (Provincial Law No. 4531)
INSTITUTIONS: Institution(s): Provincial Government of Rio Negro
DESCRIPTION: Argentina has created a “Certificate of Social and Environmental Responsibility” under Law No. 4531 to promote socially and environmentally responsible behavior by companies carrying out activities in the Province of Rio Negro.

TITLE: Australia's National Greenhouse and Energy Reporting Act 2007
DESCRIPTION: Australia's National Greenhouse and Energy Reporting Act of 2007 creates requirements for certain companies to report and disseminate information on their annual greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions, GHG projects, energy consumption, and energy production. To determine which companies have an obligation under the Act, the Clean Energy Regulator has set two types of thresholds—facility and corporate group thresholds. The information reported is then published by the Clean Energy Regulator on their website.

TITLE: Shanghai Municipal Local Standards on Corporate Social Responsibility
DESCRIPTION: The Shanghai Municipal Local Standards on Corporate Social Responsibility (CSR) encourages companies to asses their CSR policies and report on progress.

TITLE: National Instrument 51-102 Continuous Disclosure Obligations
DESCRIPTION: Under the National Instrument on Continuous Disclosure Obligations, companies that are listed on the Toronto Stock Exchange must disclose environmental information, including disclosing policies on the company's relationship with the environment and the steps taken to implement the policy.

TITLE: Report on the Russian largest companies’ investments in green projects as per the Regulations on information disclosure No. 11-46/пз-н
INSTITUTIONS: Institution(s): Ministry of Finance of the Russian Federation
DESCRIPTION: The analytical report on the Russian largest companies’ investments in green projects summarizes data on 253 companies from the list of the 400 largest companies (by economic sector) based on their official reporting.

TITLE: Austrian Eco-label (Österreichisches Umweltzeichen) Guideline UZ 49
INSTITUTIONS: Institution(s): Federal Ministry of Agriculture, Forestry, Environment and Water Management
DESCRIPTION: The Austrian Eco-label for Sustainable Investment Funds is awarded to investment products that comply with the criteria provided in the Eco-label Guideline (UZ 49).

TITLE: Colombia's Corporate Governance Code
DESCRIPTION: Colombia's Corporate Governance Code, which is comprised of 41 best practices drawn up by participants in the country’s capital market, aims to standardise the corporate governance practices that companies have developed independently through their own internal codes.

TITLE: The UK's Climate Change Act of 2008
COUNTRY: Country: United Kingdom of Great Britain and Northern Ireland
DESCRIPTION: The United Kingdom's Climate Change Act of 2008 sets a legally binding target to reduce carbon dioxide emissions in the country by at least 80 percent by 2050, from 1990 levels, and requires the Government to set legally binding emissions targets, called carbon budgets, every five years.

TITLE: Guidance Regarding Disclosures Related to Climate Change in the United States
INSTITUTIONS: Institution(s): US Securities and Exchange Commission
DESCRIPTION: The United States Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) has published an interpretive release to provide guidance to public companies regarding the SEC's existing disclosure requirements as they apply to climate change matters.

TITLE: Resolution 3.813/2009 Supports the Expansion of Sugarcane in Agro-Ecological Zoning, While Prohibiting the Financing of its Expansion in Certain Areas
DESCRIPTION: Resolution 3.813/2009 links agro-industrial credit to the Agro-Ecological Zoning for expansion and industrialization of sugarcane. It prohibits financing for crop expansion in the Amazon and Pantanal biomes, as well as in the Upper Paraguay River Basin, among other areas.

TITLE: Provincial Law on Social and Environmental Reporting by Firms (Decreto Nº 517/11)
DESCRIPTION: The Province of Salta in Argentina adopted legislation on a framework for social and environmental reporting by firms, which provides incentives for voluntary participation.

TITLE: National Policy of Combating Climate Change
INSTITUTIONS: Institution(s): Ministry of Natural Resources & Environment
DESCRIPTION: Samoa’s National Policy on Combating Climate Change provides a framework to mitigate and adapt to the effects of climate change.

TITLE: Saudi Arabia's Risk Management Regulation Includes Provisions on Disaster Risk Management for Insurance Companies
INSTITUTIONS: Institution(s): Saudi Arabian Monetary Agency - Insurance Supervision Department
DESCRIPTION: Saudi Arabia's Risk Management Regulation stipulates that Insurance companies are required to set up disaster risk management strategies and disaster coverage within reinsurance arrangements in order to obtain licenses.

TITLE: French Regulations on Corporate Environmental and Social Reporting
DESCRIPTION: In 2012, France adopted a Decree (No. 2012-557) on the Transparency Obligations of Companies in Social and Environmental Matters, which further details requirements for companies with regards to reporting on environmental and social information.

TITLE: Bangladesh's Policy Guidelines on Green Banking
DESCRIPTION: The central bank of Bangladesh has issued policy guidelines for green banking that aim to prevent environmental degradation and ensure sustainable banking practices.

TITLE: Revised Guidance on the Scope of the Trustee Knowledge and Understanding (TKU) Requirements
COUNTRY: Country: United Kingdom of Great Britain and Northern Ireland
DESCRIPTION: The Pensions Regulator (TPR) of the United Kingdom issued revised guidance in 2009 on the scope of trustee knowledge and understanding (TKU) requirements, including the extent to which social, environmental, and ethical considerations are taken into account when making investment decisions.

TITLE: Greek Law (3487/2006) Requires Environmental and Social Reporting by Certain Companies and Financial Institutions
DESCRIPTION: In 2006, Greece adopted Law 3487/2006, which transposes the European Union Directive 2003/51/EC into national legislation and states that an analysis of environmental and social aspects necessary for “an understanding of the company’s development, performance, or position” should be included in the directors’ reports.

TITLE: Protocolo de Intenções pela Responsabilidade Socioambiental
INSTITUTIONS: Institution(s): Ministry of Environment and the Brazilian Banks Federation (FEBRABAN)
DESCRIPTION: Protocol signatories have been committed to financing development with sustainability by means of lines of credit and programs that foster the population’s standards of living and environmental protection.

TITLE: Italy's Regulation (N. 35/2010) Includes Provisions on Ethical and Socially Responsible Finance
INSTITUTIONS: Institution(s): Istituto per la Vigilanza sulle Assicurazioni
DESCRIPTION: Italy's Institute for the Supervision of Insurance (Italian Istituto per la vigilanza sulle assicurazioni, or IVASS) requires disclosures for all insurance products labeled as "ethical" or "socially responsible" under Regulation N. 35 of 26 May 2010.

TITLE: Guidelines on Disclosing How Investments Take Into Account Labour Standards or Environmental, Social, or Ethical Considerations (Regulatory Guide 65)
INSTITUTIONS: Institution(s): Australia Securities and Investments Commission
DESCRIPTION: The Australian Securities and Investments Commission's (ASIC’s) Regulatory Guide 65 sets out guidelines on how product issuers can meet their obligations under the Corporations Act of 2001 (s1013DA) to disclose in Product Disclosure Statements (PDSs) how labour standards or environmental, social, or ethical considerations are taken into account in selecting, retaining, or realising an investment.

TITLE: National Association of Insurance Commissioners (NAIC) Climate Risk Disclosure Survey
INSTITUTIONS: Institution(s): National Association of Insurance Commissioners (NAIC)
DESCRIPTION: The Insurer Climate Risk Disclosure Survey, adopted by the NAIC in 2010, was designed to be an insurer reporting mechanism that would provide regulators with a window into how insurers assess and manage risks related to climate change.

TITLE: Corporate Social Responsibility (CSR) Law No. 2594 of Buenos Aires City
DESCRIPTION: The Corporate Social Responsibility (CSR) Law 2594 in Buenos Aires, Argentina, requires all local and international companies in the city with more than 300 employees to generate annual sustainability reports.

TITLE: Indonesia's Rule on the Obligation to Submit an Annual Report for Issuers or Public Companies (Rule X.K.6) Requires Reporting on Social Responsibility
DESCRIPTION: Indonesia's Rule on the Obligation to Submit an Annual Report for Issuers or Public Companies (Rule X.K.6) requires listed companies to submit annual reports that contain a description of social responsibility activities and expenditures.

TITLE: The Canadian Environmental Protection Act Requires Large Emitters to Report Greenhouse Gas Emissions
INSTITUTIONS: Institution(s): Government of Canada, Environment and Climate Change Canada
DESCRIPTION: The Canadian Environmental Protection Act of 1999 requires companies to provide information on specific pollutant emissions for inclusion in the National Pollutant Release Inventory.

TITLE: Japan's Mandatory Greenhouse Gas Accounting and Reporting System
DESCRIPTION: Japan's Mandatory Greenhouse Gas Accounting and Reporting System requires specified entities that emit greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions above a defined threshold to calculate their GHG emissions and report the results to the Government.

TITLE: Japan's Environmentally Rated Loan Program
DESCRIPTION: The Development Bank of Japan (DBJ) initiated its Environmentally Rated Loan Program in 2004 in order to support the environmental efforts of companies.

TITLE: Brazil's National Electrical Energy Agency's (ANEEL) Requirements for Annual Sustainability Reporting (Despacho 3034/2006)
INSTITUTIONS: Institution(s): Brazilian Securities and Exchange Commission (CVM)
DESCRIPTION: The ANEEL (Brazil's National Electrical Energy Agency) Requirements for Annual Sustainability Reporting (Despacho 3034/2006) requires all energy and utility companies to disclose all social and environmental information and to produce an annual sustainability report.

TITLE: Belgium's Law on Collective Investment Portfolio Management Requires Disclosure of Social, Environmental, and Ethical Considerations
INSTITUTIONS: Institution(s): Financial Services and Markets Authority
DESCRIPTION: Under Belgium's Law on Collective Investment Portfolio Management, Article 72 requires Collective Investment Schemes to disclose in their annual reports the degree to which social, environmental, and ethical criteria are considered in their investment strategies.

TITLE: Environmental Investment Fund of Namibia Act 13 of 2001
INSTITUTIONS: Institution(s): Parliament of the Republic of Namibia
DESCRIPTION: In December 2001, the Republic of Namibia released the Act on Environmental Investment Fund, amended by State-owned Enterprises Governance Act 2 of 2006.

TITLE: Turkey's Corporate Governance Principles
INSTITUTIONS: Institution(s): Capital Markets Board of Turkey
DESCRIPTION: Turkey's issuance of its Corporate Governance Principles states that listed companies need to provide information in their annual reports on social rights, health and safety, corporate social responsibility, social and environmental performance, and in-house training initiatives.

TITLE: The United States' Energy Policy Act of 2005
DESCRIPTION: The United States' Energy Policy Act of 2005 sets out tax incentives and loan guarantees for various types of energy production.

TITLE: Belgium's Law on Supplementary Pensions Requires Disclosure of Social, Environmental, and Ethical Criteria
DESCRIPTION: Article 42 of Belgium's Law on Supplementary Pensions (Vandenbroucke Law) requires Supplementary Pension schemes to disclose in their annual reports the degree to which social, environmental, and ethical criteria are considered in investment strategy.

TITLE: The United States' Property-Assessed Clean Energy (PACE) Programs Offer Financing for Renewable Energy and Energy Efficiency in Multiple States
DESCRIPTION: The United State's Property-Assessed Clean Energy (PACE) programs offer long-term private financing for renewable energy, energy efficiency and resiliency upgrades to homes and businesses.

TITLE: Spain's Resolution of 25 March 2002 Requires Companies to Include Environment Impact Information in their Annual Accounts
DESCRIPTION: Spain's Resolution of 25 March 2002 makes it mandatory for companies to include “all significant information in relation to the prevention, reduction, and repair of the environmental impact derived from their activity” in their annual accounts.

TITLE: Kazakhstan's Code on Corporate Governance
INSTITUTIONS: Institution(s): Financial Institutions Association of Kazakhstan
DESCRIPTION: Kazakhstan's Code of Corporate Governance has seven principles to ensure fairness, honesty, responsibility, transparency, accountability, and professionalism for effective corporate governance practices.

TITLE: France's Act on Employee Savings (Loi Fabius, Act 2001-152) Requires Investors to Disclose Environmental and Social Considerations
DESCRIPTION: France's Act on Employee Savings ('Loi Fabius', Act 2001-152) requires investors to disclose in their annual reports to what extent they take environmental and social indicators into account when buying or selling stocks and securities and when exercising their shareholder rights.

TITLE: Indonesia's Regulation on Asset Quality Rating for Commercial Banks (No. 7/2/PBI/2005) Requires the Inclusion of Environmental Measures in Assessments of Business Prospects
DESCRIPTION: Indonesia's Regulation on Asset Quality Rating for Commercial Banks stipulates that, in classifying credit quality, banks are required to assess business prospects, including the environmental conservation measures pursued by the debtor.

TITLE: France's New Economic Regulations Act Requires Publicly Traded Companies to Disclose Environmental Information
DESCRIPTION: France's New Economic Regulations Act (Nouvelles Regulations Economiques, or NRE Act) requires all publicly traded companies to disclose information in their annual reports on measures taken to account for the environmental impacts of their activities.

TITLE: Italy's Legislative Decree (252/2005) on the Regulation of Supplementary Pension Schemes Requires Reporting on Social, Ethical, and Environmental Issues
DESCRIPTION: Italy's Legislative Decree (252/2005) on the Regulation of Supplementary Pension Schemes requires pension funds to include in their annual reports and their communications to investors whether and to what extent social, ethical, and environmental issues are taken into consideration (Article 6, Section 14).

TITLE: Sweden's Pension Insurance Fund Act, as Amended – The 7th Pension Fund (AP7) Must Consider Environmental & Ethical Issues
DESCRIPTION: Sweden’s seventh pension fund (AP7) must take environmental and ethical considerations into account, while not relinquishing the overall goal of a high return on capital.

TITLE: Pension Fund Disclosure Requirements to Include ESG Factors (Pensionskassengesetz – PKG 2005)
DESCRIPTION: Austria's Pension Fund Act (Pensionskassengesetz, PKG) introduced disclosure requirements for pension funds that implement an environmental, social, and governance (ESG) approach in their investments to disclose how these factors are integrated. It does not apply to pension funds that do not consider ESG.

TITLE: Australia's Corporations Act of 2001 Requires Disclosure of Environmental Considerations Taken Into Account in Investment Decision-Making
DESCRIPTION: Australia's Corporations Act of 2001 requires providers of financial products with an investment component to disclose the extent to which environmental considerations are taken into account in their investment decision-making.

TITLE: Zimbabwe’s Environmental Management Act (Chapter 20:27)
DESCRIPTION: In 2002, the Parliament of Zimbabwe enacted Environmental Management Act [Chapter 20:27] as amended to Act 6/2005. Under Part VIII of the Act, it presents establishment of the Environment Fund administrated by the Minister of Environment and Tourism.
